+-- Exam & Architectural Insight ------------------------------------------
| Objective: SY0-701 4.6 Provisioning/de-provisioning and attestation · 5.1
| Owners · 4.2 Account inventory.
| 
| Key Concepts
|   • HR is the authoritative source; aggregation pulls every app's
| accounts, correlation links each to a person.
|   • An entitlement is one permission; an access profile bundles one app's
| entitlements; a role bundles profiles for a job.
|   • Orphaned, dormant and terminated-but-enabled accounts are de-
| provisioning failures an attacker can reuse.
|   • Access certification (attestation) has the manager or entitlement
| owner re-approve access on a schedule.
|   • These are the same concepts SailPoint and Entra ID Governance use,
| shown here with generic terms.
| 
| Manual Failure Modes
|   • Leaver process disables the directory account but not the ERP or SaaS
| accounts.
|   • Service accounts created for a project with no owner, still privileged
| years later.
|   • Reviewers approving everything in seconds: the certification becomes
| paperwork, not a control.
|   • Treating an undecided item as 'keep' so access survives because nobody
| looked at it.
| 
| How to Govern an AI Agent Here
|   • An AI agent can aggregate and correlate accounts, but revoking access
| stays a human-approved, logged change.
|   • Give an agent a service account with a named human owner and least
| privilege, then certify it like any other.
|   • Agents that recommend approve/revoke must show reasons; a reviewer who
| just accepts them is rubber-stamping.
|   • Treat comments and attributes in app exports as untrusted data, never
| as instructions to the agent.
| 
| Exam Tips
|   • 'Account still active after the employee left' = de-provisioning
| failure; fix with HR-driven automation.
|   • 'Periodic review where managers confirm access' = attestation / access
| recertification.
|   • Least privilege: when a reviewer does not respond, remove the access
| (deny by default).
|   • Data/system owner decides who gets access; the custodian implements
| it.
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

| Objective: SY0-701 4.6 Provisioning/de-provisioning and attestation · 5.1
| Owners · 4.2 Account inventory.

| Key Concepts
|   • HR is the authoritative source; aggregation pulls every app's
| accounts, correlation links each to a person.
|   • An entitlement is one permission; an access profile bundles one app's
| entitlements; a role bundles profiles for a job.
|   • Orphaned, dormant and terminated-but-enabled accounts are de-
| provisioning failures an attacker can reuse.
|   • Access certification (attestation) has the manager or entitlement
| owner re-approve access on a schedule.
|   • These are the same concepts SailPoint and Entra ID Governance use,
| shown here with generic terms.
| 
| Manual Failure Modes
|   • Leaver process disables the directory account but not the ERP or SaaS
| accounts.

| years later.
|   • Reviewers approving everything in seconds: the certification becomes
| paperwork, not a control.
|   • Treating an undecided item as 'keep' so access survives because nobody
| looked at it.
| 
| How to Govern an AI Agent Here
|   • An AI agent can aggregate and correlate accounts, but revoking access
| stays a human-approved, logged change.
|   • Give an agent a service account with a named human owner and least
| privilege, then certify it like any other.
|   • Agents that recommend approve/revoke must show reasons; a reviewer who
| just accepts them is rubber-stamping.
|   • Treat comments and attributes in app exports as untrusted data, never
| as instructions to the agent.
|

|   • 'Account still active after the employee left' = de-provisioning
| failure; fix with HR-driven automation.
|   • 'Periodic review where managers confirm access' = attestation / access
| recertification.
|   • Least privilege: when a reviewer does not respond, remove the access
| (deny by default).
|   • Data/system owner decides who gets access; the custodian implements
| it.
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

+-- Exam & Architectural Insight ------------------------------------------
| Objective: SY0-701 4.6 Provisioning/de-provisioning and attestation · 5.1
| Owners · 4.2 Account inventory.
| 
| Key Concepts
|   • HR is the authoritative source; aggregation pulls every app's
| accounts, correlation links each to a person.
|   • An entitlement is one permission; an access profile bundles one app's
| entitlements; a role bundles profiles for a job.
|   • Orphaned, dormant and terminated-but-enabled accounts are de-
| provisioning failures an attacker can reuse.
|   • Access certification (attestation) has the manager or entitlement
| owner re-approve access on a schedule.
|   • These are the same concepts SailPoint and Entra ID Governance use,
| shown here with generic terms.
| 
| Manual Failure Modes
|   • Leaver process disables the directory account but not the ERP or SaaS
| accounts.
|   • Service accounts created for a project with no owner, still privileged
| years later.
|   • Reviewers approving everything in seconds: the certification becomes
| paperwork, not a control.
|   • Treating an undecided item as 'keep' so access survives because nobody
| looked at it.
| 
| How to Govern an AI Agent Here
|   • An AI agent can aggregate and correlate accounts, but revoking access
| stays a human-approved, logged change.
|   • Give an agent a service account with a named human owner and least
| privilege, then certify it like any other.
|   • Agents that recommend approve/revoke must show reasons; a reviewer who
| just accepts them is rubber-stamping.
|   • Treat comments and attributes in app exports as untrusted data, never
| as instructions to the agent.
| 
| Exam Tips
|   • 'Account still active after the employee left' = de-provisioning
| failure; fix with HR-driven automation.
|   • 'Periodic review where managers confirm access' = attestation / access
| recertification.
|   • Least privilege: when a reviewer does not respond, remove the access
| (deny by default).
|   • Data/system owner decides who gets access; the custodian implements
| it.
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

+-- Exam & Architectural Insight ------------------------------------------
| Objective: SY0-701 4.6 Provisioning/de-provisioning and attestation · 5.1
| Owners · 4.2 Account inventory.
| 
| Key Concepts
|   • HR is the authoritative source; aggregation pulls every app's
| accounts, correlation links each to a person.
|   • An entitlement is one permission; an access profile bundles one app's
| entitlements; a role bundles profiles for a job.
|   • Orphaned, dormant and terminated-but-enabled accounts are de-
| provisioning failures an attacker can reuse.
|   • Access certification (attestation) has the manager or entitlement
| owner re-approve access on a schedule.
|   • These are the same concepts SailPoint and Entra ID Governance use,
| shown here with generic terms.
| 
| Manual Failure Modes
|   • Leaver process disables the directory account but not the ERP or SaaS
| accounts.
|   • Service accounts created for a project with no owner, still privileged
| years later.
|   • Reviewers approving everything in seconds: the certification becomes
| paperwork, not a control.
|   • Treating an undecided item as 'keep' so access survives because nobody
| looked at it.
| 
| How to Govern an AI Agent Here
|   • An AI agent can aggregate and correlate accounts, but revoking access
| stays a human-approved, logged change.
|   • Give an agent a service account with a named human owner and least
| privilege, then certify it like any other.
|   • Agents that recommend approve/revoke must show reasons; a reviewer who
| just accepts them is rubber-stamping.
|   • Treat comments and attributes in app exports as untrusted data, never
| as instructions to the agent.
| 
| Exam Tips
|   • 'Account still active after the employee left' = de-provisioning
| failure; fix with HR-driven automation.
|   • 'Periodic review where managers confirm access' = attestation / access
| recertification.
|   • Least privilege: when a reviewer does not respond, remove the access
| (deny by default).
|   • Data/system owner decides who gets access; the custodian implements
| it.
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

+-- Exam & Architectural Insight ------------------------------------------
| Objective: SY0-701 4.6 Provisioning/de-provisioning and attestation · 5.1
| Owners · 4.2 Account inventory.
| 
| Key Concepts
|   • HR is the authoritative source; aggregation pulls every app's
| accounts, correlation links each to a person.
|   • An entitlement is one permission; an access profile bundles one app's
| entitlements; a role bundles profiles for a job.
|   • Orphaned, dormant and terminated-but-enabled accounts are de-
| provisioning failures an attacker can reuse.
|   • Access certification (attestation) has the manager or entitlement
| owner re-approve access on a schedule.
|   • These are the same concepts SailPoint and Entra ID Governance use,
| shown here with generic terms.
| 
| Manual Failure Modes
|   • Leaver process disables the directory account but not the ERP or SaaS
| accounts.
|   • Service accounts created for a project with no owner, still privileged
| years later.
|   • Reviewers approving everything in seconds: the certification becomes
| paperwork, not a control.
|   • Treating an undecided item as 'keep' so access survives because nobody
| looked at it.
| 
| How to Govern an AI Agent Here
|   • An AI agent can aggregate and correlate accounts, but revoking access
| stays a human-approved, logged change.
|   • Give an agent a service account with a named human owner and least
| privilege, then certify it like any other.
|   • Agents that recommend approve/revoke must show reasons; a reviewer who
| just accepts them is rubber-stamping.
|   • Treat comments and attributes in app exports as untrusted data, never
| as instructions to the agent.
| 
| Exam Tips
|   • 'Account still active after the employee left' = de-provisioning
| failure; fix with HR-driven automation.
|   • 'Periodic review where managers confirm access' = attestation / access
| recertification.
|   • Least privilege: when a reviewer does not respond, remove the access
| (deny by default).
|   • Data/system owner decides who gets access; the custodian implements
| it.
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

briefing.title: Clean up accounts in ERP, CRM and FileShare before the Q4 access review closes
briefing.situation: Internal audit found that Redbud Example Co cannot prove who owns every login in its three main applications: the ERP (finance system), the CRM (customer system) and FileShare. HR has exported its list of 10 people, and each app has exported its accounts, 25 in total. At the same time, managers have just finished the quarterly access review, and audit thinks some of them clicked 'approve' without reading.
your_task: Match every app account to a person in the HR list, by employee ID first and by email if there is no ID.
Flag accounts nobody owns, accounts of people who have left, unused accounts, extra accounts and service accounts without an owner.
Check each review decision: was the reviewer allowed to decide, was a reason given for risky access, and does the approval break a separation-of-duties rule?
Spot reviewers who approved everything too fast, and remove access that nobody decided on.
Hand the app teams one de-provisioning list of accounts and permissions to remove.
briefing.why_it_matters: A login that belongs to nobody, or to someone who has left, is an open door for an attacker and a failed audit. An access review that people rubber-stamp gives false comfort and will not satisfy auditors.
done_when: All 25 accounts have a finding and an action, and every flagged account has a written reason.
Every review item is marked KEEP, REVOKE or ESCALATE with the reason.
The reviewer who rubber-stamped is named, and completion and revocation rates are reported.
The de-provisioning list is ready for the application owners.

glossary.Identity governance and administration (: The practice and tools that track who has which access, why they have it, and whether they still need it.
glossary.Authoritative source: The system of record for who works here, usually HR, which decides whether a person exists and is active.
glossary.Correlation: Linking each application account to the person who owns it, using matching rules such as employee ID or email.
glossary.Orphaned account: An account that no current person in HR owns, so nobody is accountable for it.
glossary.Entitlement: One specific permission inside an application, such as 'approve payments'.
glossary.Access certification (attestation): A regular review where a manager or the permission's owner confirms that each person still needs their access.
glossary.Separation of duties (SoD): A rule that one person must not hold two powers that together allow fraud, such as creating a supplier and paying it.

briefing.talking_point: Reconciled 25 accounts across 3 applications against HR, flagging 13 for action (2 leavers with live access, 3 orphans, 3 unowned privileged accounts, 3 dormant and 2 duplicates), and certified 16 review items: kept 3, revoked 4 and escalated 9, including a separation-of-duties conflict (supplier creation plus payment approval), a self-review and a reviewer who approved 5 items at a median of 4 seconds each.

results: 25 total: Correlated 12, Privileged unowned 3, Orphan 3, Dormant 3, Duplicate 2, Terminated with access 2
Items: 16, completion %: 93.8, revocation rate %: 25.0, rubber stamp reviewers: E1008
lessons: Leaver process disables the directory account but not the ERP or SaaS accounts.
Service accounts created for a project with no owner, still privileged years later.
Reviewers approving everything in seconds: the certification becomes paperwork, not a control.
governance: An AI agent can aggregate and correlate accounts, but revoking access stays a human-approved, logged change.
Give an agent a service account with a named human owner and least privilege, then certify it like any other.
case_study.note: Simulated lab with fictional people, systems and data, built with the open-source IdentityOps Lab (practice aligned to the CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 exam objectives). Results come from running the lab's engine on its sample scenario.

exam_bank.stem: A company places signs at every entrance that read: "This facility is monitored 24/7 by video surveillance. Trespassers will be prosecuted." Which of the following control types do the signs BEST represent?
exam_bank.explanation: The signs are meant to discourage someone from attempting entry, which makes them a deterrent control. They do not detect anything themselves; the cameras they mention would be the detective control.

exam_bank.stem: A manufacturing plant runs a legacy controller that cannot support multifactor authentication. The security team places the controller on an isolated network segment that can be reached only through a jump server requiring MFA. Which of the following control types BEST describes this arrangement?
exam_bank.explanation: A compensating control is an alternative measure used when the required control cannot be implemented on the system itself. The segmentation does block access, but the BEST description is compensating because it substitutes for the MFA the controller cannot support.

exam_bank.stem: An organization's leadership approves a new information security policy and requires that a formal risk assessment be performed every year. Which of the following control categories do these measures fall under?
exam_bank.explanation: Policies and risk assessments are administrative oversight measures, which are managerial controls. Operational controls are the day-to-day tasks carried out by people, such as guard rounds or running awareness sessions.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following control categories includes host-based firewalls, antivirus software, and operating system file permissions?
exam_bank.explanation: Technical controls are implemented and enforced by systems, such as firewalls, anti-malware and permissions. Operational controls are carried out by people rather than by technology.

exam_bank.stem: After ransomware encrypts a file server, an administrator restores the server's data from the previous night's offline backup. Which of the following control types is the restoration from backup?
exam_bank.explanation: Corrective controls restore systems and limit damage after an incident has occurred. The backup did not stop the encryption from happening, so it is not preventive.

exam_bank.stem: A company publishes a standard stating: "Employees must store customer data only on the approved, encrypted file share." No technical mechanism enforces the rule. Which of the following control types is this?
exam_bank.explanation: A directive control instructs people what they must or must not do, such as a policy or standard. It is not preventive because nothing technically stops an employee from saving data elsewhere.

exam_bank.stem: A network sensor operating in monitoring mode generates the following entry: `ALERT: possible SQL injection from 198.51.100.24 to 10.0.5.20:443 - action: logged`. The traffic was still delivered to the server. Which of the following BEST describes this control?
exam_bank.explanation: The sensor identified and recorded the suspicious traffic but did not stop it, which is a detective control. An inline IPS that dropped the traffic would have been preventive.

exam_bank.stem: A data center installs motion sensors in its server room that sound an alarm at the guard desk whenever movement is detected after hours. Which of the following BEST describes the category and type of this control?
exam_bank.explanation: Motion sensors protect a physical space and alert staff that an event is happening, so they are physical detective controls. They do not stop anyone from entering the room, so they are not preventive.

exam_bank.stem: A security team runs monthly phishing awareness sessions, and front-desk staff check visitor identification and maintain the sign-in log each day. Which control category do these activities BEST fit?
exam_bank.explanation: Operational controls are security tasks performed by people as part of daily operations, such as awareness training and visitor checks. Managerial controls set direction and oversight, such as policies and risk assessments, rather than carrying out the tasks.

exam_bank.stem: A system administrator configures domain accounts to lock for 30 minutes after five consecutive failed login attempts. Which of the following control types does this setting represent?
exam_bank.explanation: Account lockout actively stops further password guessing, which makes it a preventive control. Lockout events may be logged, but the setting itself blocks the attack rather than only reporting it.

exam_bank.stem: A software vendor publishes a SHA-256 hash next to each installer so customers can confirm the file was not altered during download. Which of the following security concepts does this support?
exam_bank.explanation: A matching hash shows the file has not been modified, which supports integrity. A hash alone does not prove who published the file; non-repudiation requires a digital signature.

exam_bank.stem: A purchasing manager approves a large order by digitally signing it with a private key stored on a smart card. Later, the manager claims never to have approved the order. Which of the following concepts allows the company to refute this claim?
exam_bank.explanation: Non-repudiation ties an action to the holder of a private key so the signer cannot credibly deny it. The signature also provides integrity, but integrity only proves the approval was not changed, not who made it.

exam_bank.stem: A network administrator configures the RADIUS server to record each VPN user's login time, session length, and amount of data transferred. Which part of the AAA framework does this represent?
exam_bank.explanation: Accounting tracks what authenticated users do, such as session times and data usage. Authorization decides what a user is allowed to access; it does not record activity.

exam_bank.stem: A company wants its corporate wireless network to admit only company-issued laptops, regardless of which employee is signed in. Which of the following would BEST authenticate the laptops themselves?
exam_bank.explanation: Authenticating systems rather than people is typically done with machine certificates, for example through 802.1X with EAP-TLS. Passwords, biometrics and one-time codes all authenticate the user, so a personal device with valid user credentials could still connect.

exam_bank.stem: A newly hired CISO wants to compare the organization's current security controls against the requirements of a recognized security framework to identify which controls are missing. Which of the following should the CISO perform?
exam_bank.explanation: A gap analysis compares the current state with a desired state, such as a framework, and lists what is missing. A vulnerability scan finds technical weaknesses on systems but does not measure the program against a framework.

exam_bank.stem: In a zero trust architecture, which of the following components evaluates each access request against enterprise policy and threat intelligence to decide whether to grant, deny, or revoke access?
exam_bank.explanation: The policy engine makes the access decision. The policy administrator acts on that decision by setting up or tearing down the session and instructing the policy enforcement point.

exam_bank.stem: A zero trust platform has just decided to approve a contractor's request to reach an internal application. Which component is responsible for establishing the session, such as generating the session credential and instructing the gateway to open the connection?
exam_bank.explanation: The policy administrator executes the policy engine's decision by creating session credentials and signaling the enforcement point. The policy engine only makes the decision, and the enforcement point only opens or closes the connection when told to.

exam_bank.stem: In a zero trust model, a gateway sits in the data plane between users and an internal application and opens, monitors, or terminates each connection as instructed. Which of the following is this gateway?
exam_bank.explanation: The policy enforcement point is the data plane component that allows or blocks traffic between the subject and the resource. The policy engine and policy administrator are control plane components that decide and instruct but do not carry the traffic.

exam_bank.stem: A user who normally signs in from Chicago on a managed laptop attempts to log in from an unmanaged device in another country. The system evaluates this context and automatically requires an additional verification step. Which zero trust concept is being applied?
exam_bank.explanation: Adaptive identity adjusts authentication requirements based on context such as location, device and behavior. Threat scope reduction limits what a user can reach to shrink the attack surface; it does not change how the user is verified.

exam_bank.stem: In a zero trust architecture, which of the following contains the policy engine and the policy administrator?
exam_bank.explanation: The control plane holds the components that make and manage access decisions. The data plane is where traffic between subjects and resources actually flows, through the policy enforcement point.

exam_bank.stem: A security guard notices that employees often let others follow them through the badge-controlled entrance of a data center. Which of the following would BEST prevent this tailgating?
exam_bank.explanation: An access control vestibule uses two interlocking doors so only one authorized person passes at a time, which directly prevents tailgating. Video surveillance can record tailgating but does not stop it.

exam_bank.stem: A warehouse needs an intrusion sensor that detects the body heat of a person moving through an unlit storage area. Which of the following sensor types should be installed?
exam_bank.explanation: Infrared sensors detect heat signatures, so they work in the dark and respond to a warm body. Ultrasonic and microwave sensors detect motion through reflected sound or radio waves, not heat.

exam_bank.stem: A retail company is concerned that a vehicle could be driven through the glass entrance of its flagship store. The entrance must stay open to pedestrians during business hours. Which of the following would BEST address this concern?
exam_bank.explanation: Bollards are short, sturdy posts that stop vehicles while letting people walk between them. Fencing would also stop vehicles but would block the pedestrian entrance the store needs to keep open.

exam_bank.stem: A security engineer adds a fake cloud API key to a configuration file in an internal code repository. The key grants no access, but any attempt to use it triggers an immediate alert. Which of the following has the engineer deployed?
exam_bank.explanation: A honeytoken is a piece of fake data, such as a credential, whose use signals an intruder. A honeyfile is a decoy file that alerts when opened; here the alert depends on the fake key being used, not on the file being read.

exam_bank.stem: During a scheduled upgrade, a database patch causes the order-processing application to crash. Which part of the approved change request should the team follow to return the system to its previous working state?
exam_bank.explanation: The backout plan documents how to roll back a change that fails. The impact analysis predicts what a change could affect, but it does not give the steps to undo it.

exam_bank.stem: A patch for an e-commerce site requires the web service to be restarted, which will disconnect active customers. The change board schedules the work for 2:00 a.m. on Sunday, when traffic is lowest. Which of the following is the change board using?
exam_bank.explanation: A maintenance window is a pre-agreed time when changes and the restarts or downtime they cause have the least business impact. A backout plan describes how to undo the change, not when to perform it.

exam_bank.stem: Before approving a proposed firewall rule change, the change advisory board wants to understand which business applications could be disrupted and how serious the risk would be. Which of the following should be completed?
exam_bank.explanation: An impact analysis identifies what a change could affect and the risk involved, which informs the approval decision. A backout plan is still needed, but it explains how to reverse the change rather than assessing its effect.

exam_bank.stem: A company plans to replace its payroll software. The HR, finance, and legal departments all rely on payroll data and will be affected by the change. In change management terms, these departments are BEST described as which of the following?
exam_bank.explanation: Stakeholders are the people and groups affected by a change who should be consulted and informed. The change owner is the single party accountable for the change, not every department that depends on the system.

exam_bank.stem: An administrator updates a shared runtime library on an application server. Afterward, two internal applications on the same server stop working because they required the older library version. Which of the following technical implications was MOST likely not evaluated?
exam_bank.explanation: The applications relied on a specific library version, so the change broke a dependency. The applications might also be old, but the failure was caused by the unexamined relationship between components, not by their age.

exam_bank.stem: After a scheduled upgrade, users report that the new version of the accounting software will not launch. The endpoint logs show: `Execution blocked: C:\Program Files\AcctPro\acctpro.exe - hash not in approved list`. Which of the following should have been updated as part of the change?
exam_bank.explanation: The new executable has a new hash that is not in the approved list, so the allow list should have been updated with the change. A deny list blocks only listed items and would not block an unlisted program.

exam_bank.stem: A network team wants to keep every revision of its router configuration files, see exactly who changed each line, and quickly revert to any earlier revision. Which of the following BEST meets these requirements?
exam_bank.explanation: Version control tracks every revision with its author and allows rollback to any earlier version. Change documentation records what was changed and why, but it does not store each file revision or allow an instant revert.

exam_bank.stem: An administrator changed a production firewall rule without a ticket because it seemed like a minor change. Company policy requires the change advisory board to sign off on every production change before work begins. Which change management requirement did the administrator bypass?
exam_bank.explanation: Requiring the change advisory board's sign-off before implementation is the approval process. An impact analysis may also have been skipped, but the requirement the policy describes is the sign-off itself.

exam_bank.stem: A company encrypts employee laptops and must be able to recover the data if an employee leaves or forgets a passphrase. It stores copies of the encryption keys with a trusted third party. Which of the following is this practice called?
exam_bank.explanation: Key escrow means a trusted party holds copies of keys so data can be recovered when needed. Key exchange is how two parties securely share a key for a session, not how keys are stored for recovery.

exam_bank.stem: A user wants to send a confidential file to a colleague using asymmetric encryption. The user encrypts the file with the colleague's public key. Which of the following keys will decrypt the file?
exam_bank.explanation: Data encrypted with a public key can be decrypted only with the matching private key, which only the colleague holds. The public key cannot decrypt what it encrypted; that is what keeps the file confidential.

exam_bank.stem: An employee digitally signs a contract before emailing it to a client. Which of the following keys will the client use to verify the signature?
exam_bank.explanation: The signer creates the signature with their private key, and anyone can verify it with the signer's public key. The client never has the employee's private key, and the client's own keys play no part in checking the employee's signature.

exam_bank.stem: A sales team's laptops are often lost while traveling. The company wants all data on each laptop, including the operating system, temporary files, and swap space, to be unreadable if a device is stolen. Which of the following is the BEST solution?
exam_bank.explanation: Full-disk encryption protects the entire drive, including the OS, temp files and swap space. File-level encryption protects only selected files and leaves the rest of the disk readable.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following allows two parties to establish a shared secret key over an untrusted network without ever sending the key itself?
exam_bank.explanation: Diffie-Hellman is a key exchange algorithm that lets both sides derive the same secret from values exchanged in the open. Triple DES and Blowfish are symmetric ciphers that need a key both sides already share, so they cannot set up that key themselves.

exam_bank.stem: A company wants laptops to store disk encryption keys in a hardware chip on the motherboard and to confirm that the boot process has not been tampered with before releasing those keys. Which of the following should the laptops include?
exam_bank.explanation: A TPM is a chip on the motherboard that stores keys and measures the boot process so keys are released only if the system is unchanged. An HSM provides similar protection but is a separate appliance or card for servers, not a built-in laptop chip.

exam_bank.stem: A certificate authority needs a tamper-resistant, network-attached hardware appliance to generate and protect its private signing keys while performing thousands of cryptographic operations per second. Which of the following BEST meets this requirement?
exam_bank.explanation: An HSM is a dedicated, tamper-resistant appliance built for high-volume key generation, storage and signing. A TPM is a low-performance chip tied to a single device and is not designed to serve a CA's signing workload.

exam_bank.stem: A payment processor replaces each credit card number in its order database with a random value. The real card numbers are kept in a separate, secured vault and can be retrieved by mapping the random value back. Which of the following techniques is being used?
exam_bank.explanation: Tokenization swaps sensitive data for a random token that can be mapped back to the original through a protected vault. Data masking hides part of the data, such as showing only the last four digits, and is not reversed through a vault lookup.

exam_bank.stem: During a forensic investigation, an analyst finds that a departing employee emailed vacation photos to a personal account. Further analysis shows the image files contain hidden customer records. Which of the following techniques did the employee MOST likely use?
exam_bank.explanation: Steganography hides data inside another file, such as an image, so that the file looks normal. Tokenization and masking replace or hide sensitive values in a dataset; neither conceals data inside a photo.

exam_bank.stem: An analyst reviewing a leaked password database sees these two entries: `jsmith:5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99` and `mlopez:5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99`. Which of the following would have prevented identical passwords from producing identical stored values?
exam_bank.explanation: A salt adds a unique random value to each password before hashing, so identical passwords produce different hashes and precomputed rainbow tables stop working. Key stretching slows hashing down, but without a salt two identical passwords would still produce the same output.

exam_bank.stem: A developer wants to make offline brute-force attacks against stored password hashes much slower by running each password through thousands of iterations of a hashing function. Which of the following techniques does this describe?
exam_bank.explanation: Key stretching, used by algorithms such as PBKDF2 and bcrypt, repeats hashing many times to make each guess expensive. Salting makes each hash unique but on its own does not make an individual guess any slower.

exam_bank.stem: A group of shipping companies wants a shared record of transactions that is distributed among all members. Each block of records is linked to the previous one by a hash, so past entries cannot be altered without detection. Which of the following BEST describes this technology?
exam_bank.explanation: A blockchain is a distributed, open ledger in which each block contains the hash of the previous block, so any change to an earlier entry breaks the chain. A key management system stores and manages keys centrally; it is not a shared transaction record.

exam_bank.stem: A web browser must check whether a server's certificate has been revoked. Instead of downloading the CA's full list of revoked certificates, it queries the status of that single certificate and receives a response of good, revoked, or unknown. Which of the following is being used?
exam_bank.explanation: OCSP returns the real-time status of one certificate on request. A CRL is the full published list of revoked certificates that the client would have to download and search itself.

exam_bank.stem: A company hosts www.example.com, mail.example.com, and shop.example.com. It wants one certificate that will cover these and any future first-level subdomains of example.com without reissuing the certificate. Which of the following should the company request?
exam_bank.explanation: A wildcard certificate for *.example.com covers any first-level subdomain, including ones created later. A SAN certificate covers only the names listed when it is issued, so new subdomains would require a new certificate.

exam_bank.stem: An administrator runs the following command on a new web server: `openssl req -new -key web01.key -out web01.csr`. The output file will be sent to a third-party certificate authority. Which of the following is the administrator creating?
exam_bank.explanation: The command uses an existing private key to create a CSR, which carries the public key and identity information for the CA to sign. A self-signed certificate would need the -x509 option, and the private key already exists as web01.key.

exam_bank.stem: Users who connect to a new internal web portal receive browser warnings that its certificate is not trusted. The administrator generated the certificate on the server itself without involving any certificate authority. Which of the following would BEST resolve the warnings on all company devices?
choices: Enable OCSP stapling on the portal
Publish the certificate in the CA's CRL
Reissue it as a wildcard certificate
Replace it with a certificate from a trusted CA
exam_bank.answer: Replace it with a certificate from a trusted CA
exam_bank.explanation: The certificate is self-signed, so browsers cannot chain it to a root of trust; a certificate issued by a CA the devices already trust fixes this. OCSP stapling only speeds up revocation checks and does nothing for a certificate that has no trusted issuer.

exam_bank.stem: After a string of break-ins, a company installs a tall perimeter fence with a locked gate around its equipment yard. Which of the following control categories does the fence belong to?
exam_bank.explanation: A fence is a tangible barrier that restricts access to a space, so it is a physical control. It is not operational, because operational controls are activities carried out by people, such as guard patrols or training.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following control categories describes security activities that are carried out mainly by people day to day, such as staff following an incident response procedure or administrators reviewing logs each morning?
exam_bank.explanation: Operational controls are procedures that people perform as part of daily operations. Managerial controls are tempting, but they focus on oversight and planning, such as policies and risk assessments, rather than the hands-on work.

exam_bank.stem: A security manager writes a vendor risk management program that defines how suppliers are evaluated and approved before any contract is signed. Which of the following control categories BEST describes this program?
exam_bank.explanation: A program that sets how risk is evaluated and governed is a managerial (administrative) control. The evaluations staff later carry out could be operational, but the program itself is a management decision about how risk is handled.

exam_bank.stem: A cloud administrator enables encryption on all storage buckets and configures security groups so that only the web tier can reach the database tier. Which of the following control categories do these settings represent?
exam_bank.explanation: Encryption and security group rules are enforced by systems, which makes them technical controls. They are not operational, because no person has to perform an activity for them to take effect.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following is an example of a technical control?
exam_bank.explanation: A firewall rule is enforced by technology, so it is a technical control. A locked cabinet also restricts access but does so with a physical barrier, which makes it a physical control.

exam_bank.stem: After several thefts, a warehouse installs bright floodlights and highly visible cameras around its loading docks. The main goal is to make would-be thieves decide the target is not worth the risk. Which of the following control types BEST describes the lighting?
exam_bank.explanation: Lighting that makes intruders feel exposed discourages them from trying, which is a deterrent control. It does not detect anything on its own; a camera recording footage would be the detective element.

exam_bank.stem: A web application firewall is set to blocking mode and drops any request that matches a known attack signature before the request reaches the web server. Which of the following control types does this represent?
exam_bank.explanation: Dropping the malicious request stops the attack before it can succeed, which is a preventive control. If the firewall only logged or alerted on the request, it would be detective instead.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the difference between a preventive control and a deterrent control?
choices: A preventive control records an action; a deterrent blocks it
A preventive control is always technical; a deterrent is always physical
A preventive control stops an action; a deterrent only discourages it
A preventive control repairs damage; a deterrent identifies it
exam_bank.answer: A preventive control stops an action; a deterrent only discourages it
exam_bank.explanation: A preventive control physically or logically blocks the action, while a deterrent tries to change the attacker's mind. Both can be technical or physical, so the category option is wrong.

exam_bank.stem: A small business places stickers from a well-known alarm monitoring company on its front windows, even though the alarm system covers only the back office. Which of the following control types do the stickers represent?
exam_bank.explanation: The stickers aim to discourage burglars from attempting a break-in, which makes them deterrent. The alarm system itself would be detective, but the stickers detect nothing.

exam_bank.stem: To stop employees from installing unapproved software, the IT department removes local administrator rights from all standard user accounts. Which of the following control types BEST describes this change?
exam_bank.explanation: Without administrator rights, users are technically unable to install software, so the control prevents the action. A directive control would only tell users not to install software without enforcing it.

exam_bank.stem: A SIEM correlates authentication logs and raises an alert when the same account signs in from two different countries within ten minutes. Which of the following control types does the alert represent?
exam_bank.explanation: The SIEM identifies and reports suspicious activity after it occurs, which is a detective control. It is not preventive, because the sign-ins are allowed to happen; the alert only reveals them.

exam_bank.stem: After an employee falls for a phishing email, an administrator resets the employee's password and revokes all active sessions for the account. Which of the following control types BEST describes these actions?
exam_bank.explanation: Resetting the password and revoking sessions fixes the problem after the incident has happened, which makes them corrective. They do block further misuse, but their purpose here is to repair the damage of a compromise already detected.

exam_bank.stem: A file integrity monitoring tool sends an alert reporting that a system binary on a web server changed outside of any approved maintenance. Which of the following control types is the monitoring tool?
exam_bank.explanation: File integrity monitoring discovers unexpected changes and reports them, which is detective. It is not corrective, because it does not restore the original file.

exam_bank.stem: Endpoint protection software finds malware on a laptop, removes it, and rolls back the registry changes the malware made. Which of the following control types BEST describes the removal and rollback?
exam_bank.explanation: Removing the malware and undoing its changes returns the system to a good state, which is a corrective control. The software did detect the malware first, but the question asks about the cleanup action, not the discovery.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following control types has the main purpose of identifying and recording that a security event has occurred?
exam_bank.explanation: Detective controls, such as logs, alarms and intrusion detection, reveal that something happened. Corrective controls act after detection to repair or restore, so they are a different stage.

exam_bank.stem: A two-person finance office cannot separate the duties of approving and issuing payments. Instead, the owner reviews every payment at the end of each month. In this situation, which of the following control types BEST describes the owner's review?
exam_bank.explanation: The review is used because the required control, separation of duties, cannot be implemented, so it is a compensating control. A review does reveal problems like a detective control, but its role here is to stand in for the missing primary control.

exam_bank.stem: Every new employee must sign an acceptable use policy stating that personal cloud storage services must not be used for company files. No software blocks those services. Which of the following control types is this policy?
exam_bank.explanation: The policy tells people what they are expected to do without enforcing it, which is a directive control. It is not preventive, because nothing technically stops an employee from using the services.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following control types is used when a required primary control cannot be implemented, providing an alternative safeguard that reduces the same risk?
exam_bank.explanation: A compensating control is a substitute for a control that is not feasible. Corrective controls fix problems after an incident occurs, which is a different purpose.

exam_bank.stem: A vendor will not release a patch for a critical server vulnerability until next month. In the meantime, the team disables the vulnerable feature and adds an intrusion prevention signature for the exploit. Which of the following control types do these temporary measures represent?
exam_bank.explanation: The measures stand in for the patch, which cannot be applied yet, so they are compensating controls. Patching would be the corrective action; these are the alternative safeguards used until it is possible.

exam_bank.stem: During onboarding, new hires receive a written procedure instructing them to report suspicious emails by using the report button in their mail client. Which of the following control types does this procedure represent?
exam_bank.explanation: A written instruction that guides how people should act is a directive control. The reports staff send may help detect phishing, but the procedure itself directs behavior rather than detecting anything.

exam_bank.stem: A hospital deploys redundant power supplies and a failover database cluster so that clinicians can still open patient records if a server fails. Which of the following security principles is the hospital MOST directly supporting?
exam_bank.explanation: Redundancy and failover keep the records reachable when something breaks, which supports availability. Integrity is about preventing unauthorized changes to the data, which these measures do not address.

exam_bank.stem: A company encrypts its payroll database so that storage administrators who manage the underlying disks cannot read employees' salary information. Which of the following principles does this PRIMARILY protect?
exam_bank.explanation: Encryption keeps the data unreadable to people who are not authorized to see it, which protects confidentiality. It does not by itself stop someone from altering or deleting data, so integrity is not the main goal.

exam_bank.stem: An attacker on the network path intercepts a wire transfer request and changes the destination account number before it reaches the bank. Which of the following security principles has been violated?
exam_bank.explanation: Changing the content of the request is an unauthorized modification, which violates integrity. Confidentiality would be violated if the attacker only read the request without changing it.

exam_bank.stem: A legal team needs proof that a specific manager sent an email, so that the manager cannot later deny sending it. Which of the following BEST provides this assurance?
choices: Encryption with a shared symmetric key
A hash of the message body
exam_bank.explanation: A digital signature is created with the sender's private key, which only the sender holds, so it provides non-repudiation. A shared symmetric key does not work, because both parties hold the same key and either could have produced the message.

exam_bank.stem: After a user signs in successfully, the file server checks the user's group memberships to decide whether the user may open the finance share. Which of the following AAA functions is the server performing?
exam_bank.explanation: Deciding what an already verified user is allowed to access is authorization. Authentication happened earlier, when the user proved their identity by signing in.

exam_bank.stem: Two application servers call each other's APIs. Each server proves its identity with a certificate installed on it instead of a person's username and password. Which of the following does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: The identity being verified belongs to a machine, not a user, so this is system authentication. Authorization is tempting, but it decides what an identity may do after it has been authenticated.

exam_bank.stem: A company grants access to the personnel folder based on job function, so everyone in the HR department automatically receives read access when they join the team. Which of the following authorization models is this?
exam_bank.explanation: Granting permissions according to a person's job role is role-based access control. Rule-based access control applies conditions such as time of day or source address to everyone, rather than permissions tied to a role.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following BEST describes authentication?
choices: Deciding which resources an identity may use
Proving that a claimed identity is genuine
Recording what an identity did during a session
Stating an identity by entering a username
exam_bank.answer: Proving that a claimed identity is genuine
exam_bank.explanation: Authentication verifies a claimed identity, for example with a password, token or biometric. Entering a username is only identification, the claim that authentication then checks.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY output of a gap analysis?
choices: Exploitable vulnerabilities found on every network host
Differences between current and target security state
Business functions ranked by recovery priority
A history of changes made to production systems
exam_bank.answer: Differences between current and target security state
exam_bank.explanation: A gap analysis compares where the organization is with where it wants to be and lists the differences. Finding exploitable vulnerabilities is the job of a vulnerability scan or penetration test, not a gap analysis.

exam_bank.stem: A security team has just finished a gap analysis against a recognized framework and found twelve missing controls. Which of the following should the team do NEXT?
choices: Repeat the analysis against another framework
Run a penetration test against each gap
Close the project because the assessment is done
Build a prioritized plan to close the gaps
exam_bank.answer: Build a prioritized plan to close the gaps
exam_bank.explanation: The value of a gap analysis comes from acting on it, so the next step is a prioritized remediation plan. Repeating the analysis against another framework would delay fixing the gaps already identified.

exam_bank.stem: A company is about to begin a gap analysis of its security program. Which of the following must be defined FIRST?
choices: The baseline or framework to measure against
The list of owners for each remediation task
The budget for purchasing new controls
The scope of a future penetration test
exam_bank.answer: The baseline or framework to measure against
exam_bank.explanation: A gap can only be measured against a target, so the desired baseline or framework must be chosen first. Remediation owners and budgets come later, after the gaps are known.

exam_bank.stem: A healthcare company acquires a small clinic. The CISO wants to compare the clinic's existing safeguards with the parent company's security standard to find out what the clinic is missing. Which of the following should the CISO perform?
exam_bank.explanation: Comparing existing controls with a required standard to find what is missing is a gap analysis. A vulnerability assessment looks for technical weaknesses in systems, not missing controls measured against a standard.

exam_bank.stem: A zero trust design gives each user access only to the specific applications they need and segments the network so that a compromised account can reach as few resources as possible. Which of the following concepts does this BEST illustrate?
exam_bank.explanation: Limiting what any single identity can reach shrinks the area an attacker can affect, which is threat scope reduction. Adaptive identity is about adjusting authentication requirements based on context, not limiting reach.

exam_bank.stem: In a zero trust architecture, which of the following describes the area behind the policy enforcement point, where a resource is located and traffic that has passed the enforcement point is allowed to reach it?
exam_bank.explanation: The implicit trust zone is the area behind the policy enforcement point where the resource lives. The control plane holds the decision-making components, not the resources being protected.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the core principle of a zero trust model?
choices: Trust any device inside the corporate perimeter
Verify users only once when they join the VPN
Block all traffic that originates from outside networks
Verify every access request, wherever it comes from
exam_bank.answer: Verify every access request, wherever it comes from
exam_bank.explanation: Zero trust assumes no request is trusted by default and evaluates each one, whether it comes from inside or outside the network. Trusting devices inside the perimeter is the traditional model that zero trust replaces.

exam_bank.stem: A museum wants an alarm to trigger when anyone steps onto a mat placed directly in front of a valuable display case. Which of the following sensor types should be used?
exam_bank.explanation: A pressure sensor detects weight or force, such as a person stepping on a mat. Infrared sensors detect body heat in an area, which could trigger on visitors who never step in front of the case.

exam_bank.stem: A facility needs motion sensors that send out signals and detect movement from their reflections over a large area, including through thin non-metal walls. Which of the following sensor types BEST meets this need?
exam_bank.explanation: Microwave sensors emit microwave pulses, cover large areas and can pass through some non-metal materials. Ultrasonic sensors also use reflections, but sound waves do not pass through walls.

exam_bank.stem: A data center's main gate must verify visitors' identities and also handle unusual situations, such as a delivery driver who arrives without paperwork. Which of the following controls is BEST suited to this?
exam_bank.explanation: A security guard can check identity and use human judgment to handle exceptions. A badge reader can only accept or reject a badge and cannot deal with someone who has none.

exam_bank.stem: Equipment was stolen from a loading dock last week, and management wants to find out who entered the area and when. Which of the following physical controls would BEST provide this information?
exam_bank.explanation: Recorded video shows who entered the area and at what time, so it supports the investigation. Lighting helps deter intruders and improves visibility, but it records nothing on its own.

exam_bank.stem: A security team sets up a single decoy server that appears to run an outdated, vulnerable FTP service so that it can observe the techniques attackers use. Which of the following has the team deployed?
exam_bank.explanation: A single decoy system built to attract and observe attackers is a honeypot. A honeynet is a group of decoy systems working together, not one server.

exam_bank.stem: A research team builds several decoy systems, including a web server, a database server and two workstations, all connected to look like a real department's network. Which of the following BEST describes this setup?
exam_bank.explanation: A network of multiple decoy systems is a honeynet. A honeypot is a single decoy system, so it does not describe a whole connected environment.

exam_bank.stem: An administrator places a spreadsheet named "admin passwords" on a file share. The file contains no real credentials, and opening it immediately alerts the security team. Which of the following is this spreadsheet?
exam_bank.explanation: A decoy document that triggers an alert when opened is a honeyfile. A honeytoken is a fake piece of data, such as a credential or API key, that alerts when someone tries to use it rather than when a file is opened.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY benefit of deploying a honeypot on an internal network?
choices: Blocking malware before it reaches endpoints
Encrypting sensitive data stored on servers
Removing the need for an intrusion prevention system
Detecting attackers and learning their techniques
exam_bank.answer: Detecting attackers and learning their techniques
exam_bank.explanation: Legitimate users have no reason to touch a honeypot, so any activity on it reveals an attacker and shows how they operate. A honeypot does not block malware; it attracts and observes rather than prevents.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following change management elements identifies the person accountable for making sure a change is carried out and its results are verified?
exam_bank.explanation: Ownership assigns a specific person who is accountable for the change. Stakeholders are the people affected by the change, but they are not necessarily responsible for delivering it.

exam_bank.stem: A developer has finished a new feature and tested it in the staging environment. According to the company's change management process, which of the following must happen BEFORE the feature is deployed to production?
choices: Closing the change ticket in the tracker
exam_bank.explanation: Production changes must be approved before they are implemented. Updating diagrams and closing the ticket happen after the change is made, and the backout plan is used only if the change fails.

exam_bank.stem: A proposed change to the email security gateway will affect the sales, support and legal teams. Which of the following is the PRIMARY reason to identify these stakeholders before the change is approved?
choices: So the impact analysis can be skipped
So users can write the backout plan
So the maintenance window can be made much longer
So affected groups can give input and prepare
exam_bank.answer: So affected groups can give input and prepare
exam_bank.explanation: Identifying stakeholders lets the people affected raise concerns and plan for the change. It does not replace the impact analysis, which is still needed to assess risk.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following groups typically reviews requests to modify production systems and decides whether to approve or reject them?
exam_bank.explanation: The change advisory board reviews change requests, weighs their risk and approves or rejects them. Internal audit may later check that the process was followed, but it does not approve individual changes.

exam_bank.stem: Before approving a database patch, the change advisory board asks for evidence that the patch was installed in a staging environment that mirrors production and that all applications still worked afterward. Which of the following is the board asking for?
exam_bank.explanation: Evidence from installing the patch in staging and checking the applications is the test results. An impact analysis estimates what could be affected, but it does not prove the patch actually works.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following should an impact analysis for a proposed change determine?
choices: The exact commands to run during the change
The names of the users who requested it
Which systems are affected and the risk if it fails
The purchase price of the new hardware
exam_bank.answer: Which systems are affected and the risk if it fails
exam_bank.explanation: An impact analysis identifies what the change could affect and how serious a failure would be. The exact commands belong in the implementation steps or procedure, not the impact analysis.

exam_bank.stem: A patch passed every check on the developers' workstations, but the live environment includes a load balancer that those workstations do not have. After deployment, the website went down. Which of the following would MOST likely have prevented this outage?
choices: A test environment that mirrors production
A more detailed record of who owns the change
exam_bank.answer: A test environment that mirrors production
exam_bank.explanation: Testing is only reliable when the test environment matches production; the missing load balancer let the problem slip through. A longer maintenance window gives more time but would not have revealed the incompatibility.

exam_bank.stem: An impact analysis shows that a proposed firewall change could block the connection to the company's payroll provider. Which of the following should the change manager do?
choices: Approve it and wait for payroll to report issues
Implement it outside the maintenance window
Remove payroll from the stakeholder list
Address the identified risk before approval
exam_bank.answer: Address the identified risk before approval
exam_bank.explanation: The purpose of the analysis is to find risks so they can be handled, for example by revising the rule or adding an exception, before the change is approved. Approving it anyway ignores the risk the analysis just found.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of reviewing test results during change management?
choices: Proving that every stakeholder was notified
Confirming the change works without breaking other functions
Recording which person approved the change
Choosing when the maintenance window will be
exam_bank.answer: Confirming the change works without breaking other functions
exam_bank.explanation: Test results show that the change does what it should and does not cause new problems. Recording who approved the change is part of the approval process, not testing.

exam_bank.stem: A company wants every server patch to be applied the same way each time by following documented step-by-step instructions that any qualified administrator can use. Which of the following should the company create?
exam_bank.explanation: A standard operating procedure documents repeatable steps so a task is done consistently. A backout plan only covers how to undo a change that fails, not how to perform it.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following should a backout plan contain?
choices: A list of stakeholders who must approve the change
The business justification for the change
Tests that prove the original problem exists
Steps to return the system to its pre-change state
exam_bank.answer: Steps to return the system to its pre-change state
exam_bank.explanation: A backout plan describes how to reverse the change and restore the previous working state. Business justification belongs in the change request itself.

exam_bank.stem: A network upgrade has run past the end of its approved maintenance window, and the core switch is still not working correctly. According to typical change management policy, which of the following should the team do FIRST?
choices: Leave it as is and finish tomorrow
Ask users to stop using the network
exam_bank.explanation: When a change fails or exceeds its approved window, the team should roll back using the backout plan to restore service. Extending the window without approval would bypass the change process.

exam_bank.stem: Why are maintenance windows usually scheduled during periods of low system usage?
choices: To avoid the need for a backout plan
To bypass the normal approval process
To reduce the business impact of downtime
To shorten the testing phase of the change
exam_bank.answer: To reduce the business impact of downtime
exam_bank.explanation: Doing the work when few people use the system limits how much any outage affects the business. A backout plan is still needed because the change can fail at any time of day.

exam_bank.stem: An administrator adds a scripting engine to the endpoint deny list. The next night, a scheduled backup job that relies on scripts fails on every server. Which of the following should have been done during change management to prevent this?
choices: Extend the maintenance window for the change
Restart the backup service after the change
Identify applications that depend on the blocked item
Store the deny list in version control
exam_bank.answer: Identify applications that depend on the blocked item
exam_bank.explanation: Checking dependencies would have shown that the backup job needed the scripting engine before it was blocked. Version control helps track and roll back the change but would not have revealed the dependency in advance.

exam_bank.stem: A configuration change to the internal DNS service only takes effect after the DNS daemon is stopped and started again, which briefly stops name resolution for the whole company. Which of the following technical implications must the change plan account for?
exam_bank.explanation: The change requires a service restart, which causes a short outage that must be planned and communicated. An allow list controls which software may run and is not involved in this change.

exam_bank.stem: A factory runs an inventory application that is fifteen years old, is no longer supported by its vendor and is poorly documented. The team plans to upgrade the operating system beneath it. Which of the following is the MAIN risk this application presents?
choices: It will stop the board from approving the change
It will be added to the deny list automatically
It needs no testing because it has run for years
It may fail on the new system with no vendor fix
exam_bank.answer: It may fail on the new system with no vendor fix
exam_bank.explanation: Legacy applications often break on newer platforms, and without vendor support there may be no fix, so they need careful testing. Their age is a reason for more testing, not less.

exam_bank.stem: A change policy states that administrators may perform only the work described in the approved change ticket. For example, they must not also update an unrelated driver while applying an approved patch. Which of the following does this policy describe?
exam_bank.explanation: Limiting work to what was approved is a restriction on activities during the change. A maintenance window limits when the work happens, not what work is allowed.

exam_bank.stem: An update to a web-based accounting application requires the application to be restarted. Which of the following is the MOST important reason to note this in the change plan?
choices: The restart removes the need for testing
Users may lose sessions or unsaved work
The restart replaces the backout plan
exam_bank.answer: Users may lose sessions or unsaved work
exam_bank.explanation: An application restart can end active sessions and discard unsaved work, so it should be scheduled and communicated. A restart does not replace testing, approval or the backout plan.

exam_bank.stem: A planned change will take the customer portal offline for two hours. Which of the following BEST addresses this downtime as part of the change?
choices: Leave the downtime out of the documentation
Skip testing to keep the outage shorter
Turn off logging until the portal returns
Schedule it in a window and notify customers
exam_bank.answer: Schedule it in a window and notify customers
exam_bank.explanation: Planned downtime should be scheduled for a low-impact time and communicated to the people affected. Skipping testing to save time increases the risk that the outage lasts longer than planned.

exam_bank.stem: After the database servers are moved to a new VLAN, which of the following documents MUST be updated so that incident responders have an accurate picture of the environment?
exam_bank.explanation: Moving servers to a new VLAN changes the network layout, so the diagrams must be updated to match. An acceptable use policy covers how employees may use systems and is not affected by where servers sit.

exam_bank.stem: A team changed how backups are performed but did not update the written backup procedure, which still describes the old process. Which of the following is the MOST likely risk?
choices: The change advisory board is dissolved
Staff follow outdated steps during a recovery
Encryption keys are rotated too often
exam_bank.answer: Staff follow outdated steps during a recovery
exam_bank.explanation: If the procedure no longer matches reality, people who rely on it during a stressful recovery may perform the wrong steps. Outdated documentation does not affect backup speed or key rotation.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following is a PRIMARY security benefit of keeping infrastructure configuration files in a version control system?
choices: Encryption of the files while they are stored
A history of each change with the option to roll back
exam_bank.answer: A history of each change with the option to roll back
exam_bank.explanation: Version control records who changed what and when, and it lets the team return to an earlier version. It does not by itself stop unauthorized changes or replace the approval process.

exam_bank.stem: A change has been implemented and tested successfully. Which of the following should be the FINAL step in the change process?
choices: Update documentation to reflect the change
Submit the change request for review
Perform an impact analysis of the change
Obtain approval from the change board
exam_bank.answer: Update documentation to reflect the change
exam_bank.explanation: Once a change is in place and verified, the documentation is updated so it matches the new state. Submitting the request, analyzing impact and getting approval all happen before implementation.

exam_bank.stem: A team changed the firewall to allow two new ports but the documented firewall standard still lists only the old set of allowed ports. An auditor finds the mismatch. Which of the following change management steps was missed?
exam_bank.explanation: After a change, related policies and procedures must be updated so they match how systems are actually configured. The mismatch is a documentation gap; it says nothing about whether an impact analysis was done.

exam_bank.stem: In a public key infrastructure, which of the following must be kept secret by its owner and never shared?
exam_bank.explanation: The private key proves the owner's identity and decrypts data sent to them, so it must stay secret. The public key and certificate are designed to be shared freely.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the relationship between the two keys in an asymmetric key pair?
choices: Both keys are identical and held by both parties
Data encrypted with one key is decrypted with the other
The private key is published and the public one hidden
Either key can easily be calculated from the other
exam_bank.answer: Data encrypted with one key is decrypted with the other
exam_bank.explanation: In asymmetric cryptography, what one key of the pair encrypts only the other key can decrypt. Identical keys held by both parties describe symmetric encryption, not asymmetric.

exam_bank.stem: A company wants to issue each employee a certificate that ties the employee's identity to a cryptographic key, manage those certificates centrally and be able to revoke them. Which of the following should the company implement?
exam_bank.explanation: A PKI provides certificate authorities, issuance, and revocation for binding identities to public keys. A symmetric key exchange only creates shared keys and does not issue or revoke identity certificates.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY security concern with using key escrow?
choices: The escrow holder becomes a valuable target
Escrowed keys can no longer encrypt data
Key escrow makes keys shorter and weaker
Escrow prevents data from being recovered
exam_bank.answer: The escrow holder becomes a valuable target
exam_bank.explanation: Because the escrow holder keeps copies of keys, compromising it could expose many keys at once, so it must be strongly protected. Escrow exists to make recovery possible, so the option saying it prevents recovery is the opposite of its purpose.

exam_bank.stem: A company needs to encrypt several terabytes of backup data each night as quickly as possible. Which of the following is the BEST choice?
exam_bank.explanation: Symmetric algorithms such as AES are much faster than asymmetric ones, which makes them suited to large amounts of data. Asymmetric encryption is too slow for bulk data and is mainly used for key exchange and signatures.

exam_bank.stem: A clinic wants each patient's entry in its database to be encrypted with a separate key, so that if one key is exposed, only that one patient's data is at risk. Which of the following levels of encryption does this describe?
exam_bank.explanation: Encrypting each record individually limits the damage from a single key to one record. Transparent database encryption protects the whole database with one key, so exposing that key exposes every patient.

exam_bank.stem: A mobile banking app sends account data to the bank's servers, and customers often use public Wi-Fi. Which of the following BEST protects the data from eavesdroppers on the same network?
exam_bank.explanation: Transport encryption, such as TLS, protects data while it travels across the network. Database encryption protects data stored on the server and does nothing for data in transit.

exam_bank.stem: An auditor finds that a legacy site-to-site VPN still uses DES with a 56-bit key. Which of the following is the BEST recommendation?
choices: Run DES twice with the same key
Hash the DES key with MD5
exam_bank.explanation: A 56-bit key is short enough to brute-force, so the VPN should move to a modern algorithm with a longer key, such as AES-256. Running DES twice with the same key adds little strength and keeps the weak algorithm.

exam_bank.stem: Several people share a laptop. One user needs a single spreadsheet to be encrypted while all other files on the laptop remain accessible to everyone. Which of the following BEST meets this requirement?
exam_bank.explanation: File-level encryption protects just the chosen file and leaves everything else untouched. Full-disk encryption protects the entire drive but, once the system is unlocked, does not keep one file private from other users.

exam_bank.stem: A company runs dozens of cloud applications that each use encryption keys. It wants a managed service that centrally creates, rotates and stores keys, applies access policies to them and logs every use. Which of the following BEST meets this need?
exam_bank.explanation: A key management system handles the full key lifecycle, including creation, rotation, access control and auditing, across many applications. A key escrow agent only holds copies of keys for recovery and does not create, rotate or police their use, and a Trusted Platform Module is a chip in one computer and cannot manage keys for many cloud applications.

exam_bank.stem: A smartphone processes fingerprint data in an isolated area of its main processor that the operating system cannot access, even if the operating system is compromised. Which of the following is this isolated area?
exam_bank.explanation: A secure enclave is a protected, isolated area within the processor that keeps sensitive operations away from the main operating system. A TPM is a separate chip, typically on a computer's motherboard, rather than an isolated area of the main processor.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the difference between a hardware security module (HSM) and a Trusted Platform Module (TPM)?
choices: An HSM is a dedicated device for heavy key use; a TPM is a chip in one computer
An HSM stores certificates only; a TPM issues certificates to users
An HSM is software-based; a TPM is a cloud service for many systems
An HSM hashes passwords; a TPM encrypts network traffic
exam_bank.answer: An HSM is a dedicated device for heavy key use; a TPM is a chip in one computer
exam_bank.explanation: An HSM is a dedicated, often network-attached appliance built for high-volume key generation and storage, while a TPM is a chip on one device's motherboard that protects that device's keys and boot integrity. Neither is a software or cloud-only service, which rules out that option.

exam_bank.stem: Call center agents verify customers by asking for the last four digits of their card number. The agents' screens display card numbers as ****-****-****-1234. Which of the following techniques is being used?
exam_bank.explanation: Hiding most of a value while showing a part of it is data masking. Tokenization replaces the entire value with a substitute token, so no real digits would be shown.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following obfuscation techniques hides the very existence of a message by embedding it inside another file, such as an audio recording?
exam_bank.explanation: Steganography conceals data inside an ordinary-looking carrier file so that no one suspects a message is there. Data masking hides parts of a value but does not hide the fact that the data exists.

exam_bank.stem: Developers need realistic customer data in a test environment, but real names and phone numbers must not be exposed. The test data will never need to be converted back to the original values. Which of the following is the BEST approach?
exam_bank.explanation: Masking replaces sensitive values with realistic but fake ones, which is ideal when the originals never need to be recovered. Tokenization is designed to be reversible through a token vault, which adds complexity the test environment does not need.

exam_bank.stem: A mobile payment wallet stores a substitute value on the phone instead of the real card number. The substitute is useless if stolen, and only the payment network can map it back to the real card. Which of the following techniques does this describe?
exam_bank.explanation: Replacing a sensitive value with a token that can be mapped back only through a secure system is tokenization. Data masking hides part of a value for display and is not meant to be mapped back to the original for transactions.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following BEST describes a cryptographic hash function?
choices: A reversible function that uses a shared key
A one-way function with a fixed-length output
A function whose output matches the input length
A two-way function that uses a key pair
exam_bank.answer: A one-way function with a fixed-length output
