exam_bank.stem: A security researcher posts on a public forum that a company's customer database is for sale and includes a sample containing real customer records. Which of the following indicators does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: Evidence of a breach that has been posted or reported publicly is a published/documented indicator. The company's own logs played no part in this discovery, so the log-related options do not fit.

exam_bank.stem: A workstation can no longer reach its antivirus vendor's update site or the operating system's patch servers, though every other website loads normally. Someone recently edited the workstation's hosts file. Which of the following indicators does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: Malware often blocks security updates so it cannot be detected or removed, which shows up as blocked content. Nothing suggests high CPU or network use, so resource consumption does not fit.

exam_bank.stem: A hospital moves its infusion pumps to their own VLAN, with firewall rules that let only the pump management server talk to them. Which of the following mitigation techniques is being used?
exam_bank.explanation: Dividing the network into zones with controlled traffic between them is segmentation. Isolation would cut the pumps off from all other systems, but the management server can still reach them.

exam_bank.stem: A water utility keeps the engineering workstation that programs its safety controllers completely disconnected from every other network. Data is moved to it only on approved, scanned media. Which of the following mitigation techniques does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: Removing all network connections so a system cannot communicate with anything else is isolation, often called an air gap. Segmentation still allows controlled traffic between zones.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the main security benefit of network segmentation?
choices: It limits how far an attacker can move after a compromise
It encrypts all traffic between every host
It stops users from choosing weak passwords
It removes the need to patch the systems inside each network segment
exam_bank.answer: It limits how far an attacker can move after a compromise
exam_bank.explanation: Segmentation restricts which systems can reach each other, which contains lateral movement after a breach. It does not encrypt traffic or replace patching.

exam_bank.stem: An audit finds that a file share containing HR records can be read by the Everyone group. Which of the following mitigations BEST addresses this finding?
choices: Restricting share permissions to the HR group
Installing a host-based firewall on the server
Enabling full-disk encryption on the server
exam_bank.answer: Restricting share permissions to the HR group
exam_bank.explanation: Changing permissions so only HR staff can read the files directly fixes the excessive access. Full-disk encryption protects a stolen drive but does nothing to stop logged-in users from reading the share.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following BEST explains why an application allow list is more effective than a block list against brand-new malware?
choices: It scans files faster than antivirus software
Anything not approved in advance is blocked by default
It encrypts every program before it runs
exam_bank.answer: Anything not approved in advance is blocked by default
exam_bank.explanation: An allow list permits only known, approved programs, so new malware that no one has seen is still blocked. A block list stops only what has already been identified as bad.

exam_bank.stem: A web application connects to its database using the database's built-in administrator account, even though it only needs to read and add rows in two tables. Which of the following mitigation techniques should be applied?
exam_bank.explanation: Giving the application an account with only the rights it needs limits the damage if the application is compromised. Segmentation controls network paths, not the permissions an account has inside the database.

exam_bank.stem: Monthly scans show the same missing operating system updates on hundreds of laptops because users keep postponing restarts. Which of the following would BEST address this?
choices: Moving the laptops to an isolated network
Automated patch deployment with a forced restart deadline
Adding every laptop to a strict application allow list policy
exam_bank.answer: Automated patch deployment with a forced restart deadline
exam_bank.explanation: Automating patching with a firm restart deadline makes sure updates are actually applied. An allow list controls which programs run but does not fix missing operating system patches.

exam_bank.stem: Administrators often turn on an insecure legacy protocol on servers while troubleshooting and forget to turn it off again. Which of the following mitigation techniques would BEST make sure the setting does not stay enabled?
exam_bank.explanation: Configuration enforcement keeps checking systems against the approved baseline and resets settings that drift. Patching fixes software flaws, but it does not undo a setting an administrator changed.

exam_bank.stem: A company retired a web application but left its DNS record pointing to a cloud address it no longer owned. An attacker claimed that address and hosted a phishing page under the company's subdomain. Which of the following processes was done poorly?
exam_bank.explanation: Proper decommissioning removes every trace of a retired system, including DNS records, so nothing is left for attackers to take over. There was no software flaw to patch; the problem was a leftover record.

exam_bank.stem: The security team wants a tool on every laptop that records process, file and network activity, lets analysts investigate remotely and can cut a laptop off from the network with one click. Which of the following BEST meets these requirements?
exam_bank.explanation: Endpoint detection and response records detailed activity, supports remote investigation and can contain a device. A HIPS blocks suspicious behavior, but it does not provide the investigation and response features described.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following mitigations would BEST help a security team notice an attacker using valid stolen credentials at unusual hours?
exam_bank.explanation: Monitoring and alerting on login activity can spot valid accounts being used at odd times or places. An allow list controls which programs run and would not notice a legitimate login.

exam_bank.stem: A database server should accept connections only from two application servers, including blocking other hosts on its own subnet that never pass through the network firewall. Which of the following BEST meets this requirement?
exam_bank.explanation: A host-based firewall filters traffic on the server itself, so it can block neighbors on the same subnet. Antivirus looks for malicious files and does not filter which hosts may connect.

exam_bank.stem: A security engineer is choosing between a host-based intrusion detection system (HIDS) and a host-based intrusion prevention system (HIPS) for critical servers. Which of the following is the PRIMARY difference?
choices: A HIPS works only with encrypted network traffic
A HIPS checks only network traffic; a HIDS only files
A HIDS does not need any software on the server
A HIPS can block what it detects; a HIDS only alerts
exam_bank.answer: A HIPS can block what it detects; a HIDS only alerts
exam_bank.explanation: Both watch activity on the host, but only the prevention system can stop it automatically. Both are installed on the host, so the claim that a HIDS needs no software is false.

exam_bank.stem: A hardening review finds that servers still accept Telnet and SMBv1 connections, although SSH and newer SMB versions are available and in use. Which of the following hardening steps is BEST?
choices: Moving the servers to an isolated network
exam_bank.explanation: Turning off old protocols that are no longer needed removes known weaknesses without affecting users. Isolating the servers would cut off the services users rely on.

exam_bank.stem: A company sends backup tapes to an offsite vault by courier. It wants to make sure the data cannot be read if a tape is lost on the way. Which of the following mitigations BEST meets this goal?
choices: Applying least privilege to backup operators
Disabling unused ports on the backup server
exam_bank.explanation: Encryption keeps the data unreadable to anyone without the key, even if the tape is lost. Segmentation and least privilege protect systems on the network, not a tape in a courier's van.

exam_bank.stem: A workstation security baseline requires removing preinstalled trial programs and unused browser plug-ins. Which of the following is the PRIMARY benefit of this step?
choices: It removes the need for patching
It encrypts the data on the drive
exam_bank.explanation: Every installed program is code that could contain a flaw, so removing unneeded software leaves fewer targets. Remaining software still needs patching, so this does not replace it.

exam_bank.stem: Attackers learn that engineers at a defense contractor often read a small industry forum during lunch. They plant malicious code on that forum instead of emailing the engineers directly. Which of the following attack types does this describe?
exam_bank.explanation: A watering hole attack compromises a site the target group already trusts and visits, then waits for them to arrive. Typosquatting is tempting because it also involves a website, but it relies on a look-alike domain that victims mistype, not on infecting a real site they use.

exam_bank.stem: A company is moving its line-of-business servers to virtual machines hosted by an IaaS provider. Under the shared responsibility model, which of the following tasks will remain the company's responsibility?
exam_bank.explanation: In IaaS the customer owns everything from the guest OS upward, so OS patching stays with the customer. The hypervisor is tempting, but it sits below the guest and is maintained by the provider.

exam_bank.stem: A sales team uses a SaaS customer relationship management platform. The security manager is reviewing the vendor's responsibility matrix. Which of the following will the company MOST likely still be responsible for?
choices: Managing user accounts and access rights
exam_bank.answer: Managing user accounts and access rights
exam_bank.explanation: Even in SaaS, the customer controls who can log in and what they can see, so identity and access management stays with the customer. Patching the application is tempting, but in SaaS the provider owns the application stack.

exam_bank.stem: An organization keeps its customer database in its own data center but runs its public web front end on a public cloud provider. Which of the following BEST describes this deployment model?
exam_bank.explanation: Combining on-premises or private infrastructure with public cloud services is a hybrid cloud. Multi-cloud is the tempting distractor, but it means using more than one public cloud provider, which is not described here.

exam_bank.stem: A DevOps team now defines servers, network settings and firewall rules in version-controlled templates that a pipeline applies automatically to every environment. Which of the following security benefits does this practice MOST directly provide?
choices: Removal of the operating system attack surface
Automatic encryption of all stored data
exam_bank.explanation: Infrastructure as code builds every environment from the same reviewed templates, which keeps configurations consistent and makes drift easy to detect. Removing the OS attack surface describes serverless, not IaC.

exam_bank.stem: A developer deploys code as functions that run only when an event triggers them, and the team never provisions or manages any servers. Which of the following security tasks shifts MOST to the cloud provider in this model?
choices: Patching the underlying OS and runtime
Validating all input passed to the functions
Assigning least-privilege permissions to the functions
Reviewing the functions' own code for flaws
exam_bank.answer: Patching the underlying OS and runtime
exam_bank.explanation: In serverless computing the provider manages the servers, OS and runtime, so their patching moves to the provider. Input validation is tempting, but the customer still owns the function code and everything it does with input.

exam_bank.stem: A company is breaking a large monolithic application into dozens of small, independently deployed services that talk to each other over APIs. Which of the following is the MOST significant new security consideration?
choices: A single failure taking down the whole application
More service-to-service APIs that must be secured
One shared code base for every function
exam_bank.answer: More service-to-service APIs that must be secured
exam_bank.explanation: Microservices multiply the number of network-exposed interfaces, so each API needs authentication, authorization and encryption. A single failure taking down everything is a weakness of the monolith that microservices reduce.

exam_bank.stem: A chemical plant must ensure that its safety control network cannot be reached from any other network by any path, including through firewalls or routers. Which of the following BEST meets this requirement?
exam_bank.explanation: Only an air gap provides physical isolation with no network connection at all. VLANs and micro-segmentation are logical controls that still share connected infrastructure, so a misconfiguration could create a path.

exam_bank.stem: A company wants to separate guest wireless traffic from corporate traffic on its existing switches without buying any new hardware. Which of the following should the network team implement?
choices: Port mirroring on the access switches
exam_bank.explanation: VLANs logically separate traffic on shared switches with no new hardware. Physical isolation would also separate the traffic, but it requires additional switches, which the requirement rules out.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following separates the control plane from the data plane so that a data center network can be configured programmatically from a central controller?
exam_bank.explanation: SDN decouples the control plane, which decides how traffic flows, from the data plane, which forwards it, and manages it through a central controller. SASE is a cloud-delivered security service for users, not a way to program data center switching.

exam_bank.stem: A company is consolidating authentication, logging and policy management for all of its branch offices into a single headquarters data center. Which of the following is the MOST likely security drawback of this centralized design?
choices: Policies become harder to apply consistently
It can create a single point of failure
Logs end up scattered across many systems
Each site needs its own administrators
exam_bank.answer: It can create a single point of failure
exam_bank.explanation: Centralizing services improves consistency and visibility, but if the central site fails, every branch loses the service. Inconsistent policy and scattered logs are weaknesses of decentralized designs, not centralized ones.

exam_bank.stem: A security architect is comparing containers with virtual machines for hosting several customer workloads on one server. Which of the following is the MOST important security difference?
choices: Containers share the host operating system kernel
Containers each require a full guest operating system
Containers cannot be scanned for vulnerabilities
Containers must run on a type 1 hypervisor
exam_bank.answer: Containers share the host operating system kernel
exam_bank.explanation: Containers share the host kernel, so a kernel flaw or container escape can affect every container on the host, while VMs each run their own kernel on a hypervisor. A full guest OS per instance describes VMs, not containers.

exam_bank.stem: An audit of a company's virtualization platform finds dozens of virtual machines that developers created for short tests and never removed. Most are unpatched and no one knows who owns them. Which of the following BEST describes this issue?
exam_bank.explanation: VM sprawl is the uncontrolled growth of unmanaged virtual machines that miss patching and monitoring. VM escape is an attack that breaks out of a guest to reach the hypervisor, which is not what the audit found.

exam_bank.stem: A company is installing smart thermostats and door sensors in its offices. The devices use hard-coded credentials and the vendor provides no way to install security software on them. Which of the following would BEST reduce the risk they pose?
choices: Install endpoint detection agents on the devices
Enable full-disk encryption on the devices
Join the devices to the corporate domain
Place the devices on an isolated network segment
exam_bank.answer: Place the devices on an isolated network segment
exam_bank.explanation: Many IoT devices cannot be hardened or run agents, so isolating them limits what an attacker can reach if one is compromised. Installing EDR agents sounds strong but is not possible on devices that cannot run added software.

exam_bank.stem: A municipal water utility is designing security for the SCADA systems that control its pumps and treatment chemicals. Which of the following should be the PRIMARY design priority?
choices: Availability and safety of the physical process
Data sovereignty of the historian data
exam_bank.answer: Availability and safety of the physical process
exam_bank.explanation: ICS and SCADA environments control physical processes, so keeping them running safely outweighs other goals. Confidentiality is the usual IT priority, but leaking sensor readings is far less harmful than a pump or dosing failure.

exam_bank.stem: A medical infusion pump must react to sensor readings within a few milliseconds every time, or a patient could be harmed. Which of the following is the pump MOST likely running?
exam_bank.explanation: An RTOS guarantees that tasks finish within strict, predictable time limits, which safety-critical devices need. A type 2 hypervisor adds a layer of overhead and unpredictable scheduling, which is the opposite of what the pump needs.

exam_bank.stem: A manufacturer's production line relies on an embedded controller whose vendor no longer releases firmware updates. The controller cannot be replaced until next year. Which of the following is the BEST way to reduce the risk until then?
choices: Apply operating system patches to it manually
Install host-based antivirus on the controller
Segment the controller and restrict traffic to it
Enable automatic updates on the controller
exam_bank.answer: Segment the controller and restrict traffic to it
exam_bank.explanation: When a device cannot be patched, compensating controls such as network segmentation and strict access rules reduce exposure. Manual patching or automatic updates are not options because no patches are available.

exam_bank.stem: A CFO supports moving card processing to a third-party payment provider because the provider will contractually take on liability for breaches of the payment environment. Which of the following architecture considerations is the CFO relying on?
exam_bank.explanation: Shifting the financial impact of a risk to another party through a contract is risk transference. Ease of recovery concerns how quickly a system can be restored, not who pays when something goes wrong.

exam_bank.stem: A defense contractor must keep complete physical control of the servers that store classified designs, and its policy forbids any provider staff from having access to the hardware. Which of the following deployment models BEST meets this requirement?
exam_bank.explanation: Only on-premises infrastructure keeps the hardware entirely under the organization's own physical control. A community cloud is shared by several organizations with similar needs, so physical control of the hardware is shared with other members or with a third-party operator rather than held by the contractor alone.

exam_bank.stem: A company is deploying a public web server and wants to keep internet users from ever reaching the internal network directly. Where should the web server be placed?
exam_bank.explanation: A screened subnet sits between the internet and the internal network, so public services are reachable without exposing internal hosts. Placing the server on any internal segment would let a compromise of the server reach internal systems directly.

exam_bank.stem: A firewall protects the network segment that holds a payment database. Policy states that if the firewall crashes, no traffic may pass to the database until the firewall is restored. Which of the following failure modes does this describe?
exam_bank.explanation: Fail-closed means the device blocks all traffic when it fails, which protects confidentiality at the cost of availability. Fail-open would let traffic through unchecked during a failure, which the policy forbids.

exam_bank.stem: A hospital is adding an inline IPS in front of its patient portal. Leadership requires that the portal stay reachable even if the IPS hardware fails, but the IPS must still block attacks when it is working. Which of the following BEST meets these requirements?
choices: Configure the IPS to fail closed
Connect the IPS to a SPAN port
Configure the IPS to fail open
Replace the IPS with a passive IDS
exam_bank.answer: Configure the IPS to fail open
exam_bank.explanation: Fail-open lets traffic bypass a failed inline device, preserving availability while keeping prevention during normal operation. A SPAN port or passive IDS would also keep the portal up, but they cannot block attacks, so they miss the second requirement.

exam_bank.stem: A security analyst wants to inspect production traffic for threats without any chance that the monitoring tool will block or delay that traffic. Which of the following deployments should the analyst choose?
choices: A passive sensor connected to a network tap
A reverse proxy in front of the servers
exam_bank.answer: A passive sensor connected to a network tap
exam_bank.explanation: A passive sensor on a tap receives a copy of the traffic, so it can never block or slow production flows. An inline IPS sits in the traffic path, so a failure or false positive could disrupt traffic.

exam_bank.stem: A security device generated this alert: `SQL injection attempt 198.51.100.23 -> 10.0.5.20:443 action=alert`. The malicious request still reached the server. Management wants such requests stopped automatically in the future. Which of the following should replace the current device?
exam_bank.explanation: An IPS sits inline and can drop malicious traffic, while the alert-only behavior shows the current device is acting as an IDS. Another IDS would detect the attack again but still let it reach the server.

exam_bank.stem: Administrators must manage servers in a high-security zone, but policy prohibits direct remote desktop connections from user workstations to those servers. Which of the following should be implemented?
exam_bank.explanation: A jump server is a hardened, monitored host that administrators connect to first, and only it is allowed to reach the secure zone. A reverse proxy publishes services to clients; it is not a controlled administrative entry point.

exam_bank.stem: A company wants all employee web requests to pass through a device that filters URLs by category, caches common content and hides internal client addresses from websites. Which of the following should be deployed?
exam_bank.explanation: A forward proxy acts for internal clients making outbound requests and can filter, cache and hide their addresses. A reverse proxy does similar work, but for inbound requests to the company's own servers.

exam_bank.stem: An e-commerce site runs on four identical web servers. The company wants incoming requests spread evenly across them and any server that fails a health check removed from service automatically. Which of the following should be deployed?
exam_bank.explanation: A load balancer distributes client requests across a pool of servers and uses health checks to stop sending traffic to failed ones. A WAF inspects HTTP traffic for attacks but does not spread load or track server health.

exam_bank.stem: A company wants any device plugged into an office network jack to be denied access until the user or device authenticates against a RADIUS server. Which of the following should be implemented on the switches?
choices: MAC address filtering on each port
Port mirroring to a monitoring sensor
DHCP snooping on the access VLANs
exam_bank.explanation: 802.1X keeps a switch port in an unauthorized state until the supplicant authenticates through the authenticator to a RADIUS server. MAC filtering also restricts ports, but it checks an easily spoofed address and does not authenticate against RADIUS.

exam_bank.stem: A company is deploying 802.1X on its wireless network and requires that both the client and the authentication server prove their identity with digital certificates. Which of the following EAP methods should be used?
exam_bank.explanation: EAP-TLS requires certificates on both the client and the server for mutual authentication. PEAP is the most tempting choice, but it normally uses only a server certificate and authenticates the user with a password inside the tunnel.

exam_bank.stem: Web server logs show many requests containing `' OR 1=1 --` and `<script>` strings aimed at a customer portal. Which of the following would BEST block these attacks?
exam_bank.explanation: A WAF inspects HTTP requests and blocks application attacks such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting. A layer 4 firewall filters on IP addresses and ports, so it cannot see the malicious content inside allowed HTTPS requests.

exam_bank.stem: A small business with one IT employee wants a single appliance that provides firewalling, antivirus scanning, content filtering, spam filtering and VPN termination, all managed from one console. Which of the following BEST meets this need?
exam_bank.explanation: A UTM appliance combines many security functions in one box, which suits small organizations with limited staff. A WAF protects web applications only and offers none of the other required functions.

exam_bank.stem: A company must block an unapproved file-sharing application that tunnels its traffic over TCP 443, while still allowing normal HTTPS browsing. Which of the following firewall capabilities is required?
exam_bank.explanation: Only a layer 7 firewall can identify the application inside the traffic and block it while allowing other HTTPS. Layer 4 filtering sees only TCP 443, so it would have to allow or block all HTTPS together.

exam_bank.stem: A security engineer is hardening a new Linux server that will only serve a single internal API. Which of the following would BEST reduce the server's attack surface?
choices: Forward all of the server's logs to the SIEM
Place a network tap beside the server's switch port
Disable unneeded services and close unused ports
Increase the server's log retention to one year
exam_bank.answer: Disable unneeded services and close unused ports
exam_bank.explanation: Removing unneeded services and open ports eliminates entry points an attacker could use, which directly shrinks the attack surface. Forwarding logs to a SIEM improves detection, but every exposed service would still be there to attack.

exam_bank.stem: Two company offices need a permanent encrypted connection between their edge routers so that all traffic between the sites is protected automatically, without any software on user computers. Which of the following should be used?
choices: A jump server at each site
exam_bank.explanation: A site-to-site IPSec VPN creates a permanent tunnel between the gateways, so traffic between the sites is protected without client software. A remote access VPN connects individual users, which is not what the offices need.

exam_bank.stem: Employees who travel often stay in hotels whose networks allow only outbound HTTPS. Their IPSec VPN client fails to connect from these locations. Which of the following would BEST allow them to connect securely?
choices: An IPSec tunnel in transport mode
exam_bank.explanation: A TLS VPN runs over TCP 443, which restrictive networks usually allow, so remote users can still build an encrypted tunnel. Switching IPSec to transport mode changes what is encrypted, but it still uses protocols the hotel network blocks.

exam_bank.stem: A retailer with 300 stores wants to replace expensive MPLS circuits with ordinary broadband and LTE links. It wants central management and automatic routing of each application over the best-performing link. Which of the following BEST meets these requirements?
exam_bank.explanation: SD-WAN centrally manages several WAN links and steers traffic over them based on application performance. SASE is the tempting choice because it can include SD-WAN, but its focus is cloud-delivered security for users rather than link selection between sites.

exam_bank.stem: Most of a company's employees now work remotely and connect straight to SaaS applications. The company wants a cloud-delivered service that combines secure web gateway, CASB, zero trust network access and firewall functions close to each user. Which of the following should it adopt?
exam_bank.explanation: SASE delivers networking and security services such as SWG, CASB, ZTNA and firewall-as-a-service from the cloud, close to users wherever they work. A UTM bundles similar functions, but in an on-premises appliance that remote users would have to route back through.

exam_bank.stem: A clinic stores patient diagnoses and treatment histories that are covered by HIPAA. Which of the following BEST describes this type of data?
exam_bank.explanation: Data whose handling is governed by laws such as HIPAA is regulated data. Intellectual property is tempting because the data is valuable, but IP refers to creations such as inventions or designs, not patient records.

exam_bank.stem: A beverage company has never patented its drink formula. Instead, only three employees know it, and each has signed a confidentiality agreement. Which of the following data types BEST describes the formula?
exam_bank.explanation: A trade secret is valuable business information protected by keeping it confidential rather than by registering it. It is not regulated data, because no law dictates how the formula must be handled.

exam_bank.stem: A company's DLP system detects sensitive data in documents and email text, but it misses the same data when it is encoded in barcodes and serialized binary files. Which of the following types of data is the DLP system failing to inspect?
exam_bank.explanation: Barcodes and binary formats are non-human-readable, so they need decoding before their content can be inspected. Human-readable data such as document text is exactly what the DLP system is already catching.

exam_bank.stem: A marketing team publishes product brochures and press releases on the company website for anyone to download. Which of the following data classifications should these documents have?
exam_bank.explanation: Information intended for release to anyone carries the public classification and needs no confidentiality controls. Private is tempting as the opposite label, but it applies to information about individuals that should not be disclosed.

exam_bank.stem: A company labels its order-processing database so that it receives the strongest backup and availability protections, because business operations stop if the data becomes unavailable. Which of the following classifications BEST fits this data?
exam_bank.explanation: Critical data is data the organization cannot operate without, so it gets the highest availability protections. Confidential and restricted focus on limiting who can see data, which is not the concern described.

exam_bank.stem: An analytics application loads customer records into memory and decrypts them so it can calculate monthly trends. Which of the following states is the data in while it is being calculated?
exam_bank.explanation: Data that is loaded in memory and actively processed is data in use. Data at rest is tempting because the records came from a database, but once they are decrypted in memory and being processed, they are in use.

exam_bank.stem: A company wants to protect customer records as they move across the internal network between its application servers and its database servers. Which of the following should it implement?
choices: Enable full-disk encryption on the database servers
Hash the customer records in the database
Mask the records in the database tables
Enable TLS on the database connections
exam_bank.answer: Enable TLS on the database connections
exam_bank.explanation: TLS encrypts the connection, which protects data in transit between the servers. Full-disk encryption protects data at rest on the disks and does nothing for data crossing the network.

exam_bank.stem: A German company learns that its cloud provider may copy backup data to data centers in another country. The legal team is concerned that the data could then be subject to that country's laws and government access requests. Which of the following concepts is the legal team concerned about?
exam_bank.explanation: Data sovereignty means data is subject to the laws of the country where it is physically stored. Data retention concerns how long data is kept, not which country's laws apply.

exam_bank.stem: Logs for a bank's administrative portal show successful logins from IP addresses in countries where the bank has no staff or customers. The bank wants to deny any login attempt that geolocation places outside its country of operation. Which of the following methods should it use?
exam_bank.explanation: Geographic restrictions use the location of a request to allow or deny access, which matches the requirement. Segmentation separates internal networks but does not consider where a remote user is located.

exam_bank.stem: A developer needs to store user passwords so that the original passwords cannot be recovered from the database, even by administrators. Which of the following should the developer use?
exam_bank.explanation: A salted hash is a one-way function, so the original password cannot be recovered, but a login attempt can still be checked by hashing it again. Encryption is reversible by anyone holding the key, which defeats the requirement.

exam_bank.stem: Call center agents need to confirm a customer's identity, but their screens show card numbers only as `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-4821`. The full number remains stored in the back-end system. Which of the following methods is being used?
exam_bank.explanation: Masking hides part of a value when it is displayed while the original stays intact in storage. Tokenization replaces the stored value itself with a surrogate held in a vault, which is not what this display shows.

exam_bank.stem: A merchant wants to take its order database out of PCI DSS scope while still letting the order system reference each customer's card for refunds. Its payment processor will keep the real card numbers and return a surrogate value for each one that cannot be reversed without access to the processor's vault. Which of the following methods should the merchant use?
exam_bank.explanation: Tokenization replaces card numbers with surrogates that have no mathematical relationship to the originals, and only the processor's vault can map them back, so the merchant's database no longer holds cardholder data and drops out of PCI DSS scope. Encryption is tempting, but encrypted card numbers are still cardholder data, and the merchant would have to manage the key, which keeps the database in scope.

exam_bank.stem: A software company ships a JavaScript application and wants to make the code difficult for competitors to read and reverse engineer, while the code must still run normally in customers' browsers. Which of the following should the company use?
exam_bank.explanation: Obfuscation makes code hard for humans to understand while leaving it executable. Encryption would also hide the code, but browsers could not run it without first decrypting it, which defeats the purpose.

exam_bank.stem: A retailer wants to shrink the number of systems in scope for PCI DSS audits. It plans to move all systems that store or process cardholder data into a separate network zone with tightly controlled access. Which of the following data protection methods is this?
exam_bank.explanation: Segmentation isolates the systems that handle sensitive data, so fewer systems fall into audit scope. Geographic restrictions limit access by user location; they do not separate systems from one another.

exam_bank.stem: Two database servers share the same storage. If the active server fails, the second server automatically takes over the database service with the same identity and data. Which of the following BEST describes this configuration?
exam_bank.explanation: Clustering groups servers so that a standby node takes over a service when the active node fails. Load balancing spreads requests across several independent servers, but it does not move one server's service and identity to another.

exam_bank.stem: A company needs a recovery site that already has hardware and network connectivity installed but must load recent backups before it can operate. The company can accept recovery taking one to two days and has a moderate budget. Which of the following site types BEST fits?
exam_bank.explanation: A warm site has equipment and connectivity ready but needs current data restored, so it balances cost against recovery time. A hot site would recover faster, but it keeps live data synchronized and costs more than this requirement justifies.

exam_bank.stem: A company's primary data center and its backup data center are 10 miles apart. A single hurricane caused extended outages at both sites. Which of the following should the company have considered when choosing the backup location?
exam_bank.explanation: Geographic dispersion places recovery sites far enough apart that one regional disaster cannot affect both. Clustering adds redundant servers, but if those servers share the same region, the hurricane still takes them out.

exam_bank.stem: A flaw in one vendor's firewall firmware caused every firewall in the company to crash at the same moment, because all of them were the same model running the same version. Which of the following would have MOST reduced the impact?
exam_bank.explanation: Using products from different vendors means a single flaw cannot disable every device at once. Geographic dispersion would not help, because identical firewalls in distant locations would still share the same flaw.

exam_bank.stem: A company runs all of its applications with one cloud provider. During a provider-wide control plane outage that affected every region, all of the company's services went down. Which of the following would BEST prevent a repeat of this outage?
choices: A hybrid cloud with on-premises file shares
Vertical scaling of the existing servers
exam_bank.explanation: A multi-cloud design runs services with more than one provider, so one provider's outage does not stop everything. Additional availability zones are tempting, but they belong to the same provider, and this outage affected all of its regions.

exam_bank.stem: During a regional flu outbreak, half of a company's IT staff were out sick, and the only two people who knew how to restore the backup system were both unavailable. Which of the following areas of capacity planning was overlooked?
exam_bank.explanation: Capacity planning for people means having enough trained staff, cross-training and documentation to cover absences. The technology and infrastructure were working fine; the gap was that too few people could operate them.

exam_bank.stem: Department managers meet in a conference room and talk through how they would respond to a ransomware attack, step by step, without touching any production systems. Which of the following types of exercises is this?
exam_bank.explanation: A tabletop exercise is a discussion-based walk-through of a scenario that uses no systems. A simulation is the tempting choice, but it acts out the scenario with realistic events or systems rather than only talking through it.

exam_bank.stem: To validate its disaster recovery plan, a bank runs the same live transaction workload on its recovery systems at the same time as production and compares the results, without interrupting production. Which of the following types of tests is this?
exam_bank.explanation: Parallel processing runs the recovery systems alongside production on real workloads to confirm that they produce the same results. A failover test actually shifts production to the backup, which the bank deliberately avoided.

exam_bank.stem: An operations team deliberately shuts down the primary web cluster during a maintenance window to confirm that traffic automatically moves to the secondary cluster at another site. Which of the following tests is the team performing?
exam_bank.explanation: A failover test forces the primary to go offline so the team can confirm that the secondary takes over. Parallel processing runs both environments at once without taking the primary down.

exam_bank.stem: Before applying a risky patch, an administrator wants to capture the exact current state of a virtual machine so that it can be rolled back within minutes if the patch fails. Which of the following should the administrator use?
exam_bank.explanation: A snapshot captures a VM's state at a point in time and allows a fast rollback. Replication is tempting, but it copies changes, including a bad patch, to another location rather than preserving the earlier state.

exam_bank.stem: Ransomware encrypted a file server, and the encrypted files were copied to the disaster recovery site within seconds, corrupting it as well. Which of the following would BEST ensure that the company can recover from a similar attack in the future?
choices: Additional RAID mirroring on the server
More frequent snapshots on the same storage
exam_bank.explanation: Offline, offsite backups cannot be reached by ransomware on the network, so a clean copy survives. Synchronous replication is what spread the encrypted files in the first place, so adding more of it would repeat the problem.

exam_bank.stem: A database records every change to a separate log before writing it to the data files. After a crash, the administrator replays the log to restore the database to the moment just before the failure. Which of the following is being used?
exam_bank.explanation: Journaling writes each change to a log that can be replayed to rebuild the database to a precise point in time. Differential backups capture changes since the last full backup, but only as often as they run, not up to the moment of failure.

exam_bank.stem: A company ships its weekly backup tapes to a third-party storage facility. The auditor is concerned that a tape could be lost or stolen in transit and the data read. Which of the following should the company do?
choices: Increase the frequency of the backups
Enable journaling on the source servers
Encrypt the backups before they leave the site
exam_bank.answer: Encrypt the backups before they leave the site
exam_bank.explanation: Encrypting the backups means a lost or stolen tape cannot be read without the key. Increasing backup frequency improves the recovery point, but it does nothing to protect the data on a tape that goes missing.

exam_bank.stem: A data center has a diesel generator that takes about 30 seconds to start and stabilize after a utility power failure. Which of the following is needed to keep the servers running during that gap?
choices: Dual power supplies in each server
exam_bank.explanation: A UPS supplies battery power instantly, which bridges the gap until the generator takes over the load. Dual power supplies protect against the failure of one supply or circuit, but both would lose power together when utility power fails.

exam_bank.stem: A startup wants to rent virtual servers, storage and networking from a provider, but it will install, patch and manage its own operating systems and applications. Which of the following cloud service models BEST fits this plan?
exam_bank.explanation: IaaS gives the customer raw compute, storage and networking while the customer manages everything from the operating system up. PaaS is tempting, but in PaaS the provider manages the operating system and runtime, so the startup would not control them.

exam_bank.stem: A company extends its on-premises directory and file servers into a public cloud. A review finds that password rules, logging settings and firewall policies differ between the two environments. Which of the following is the MOST significant hybrid cloud challenge shown here?
choices: Losing physical control of the on-premises servers
Keeping security policies consistent across environments
Being unable to encrypt data stored in the public cloud
Being unable to use multifactor authentication on premises
exam_bank.answer: Keeping security policies consistent across environments
exam_bank.explanation: A hybrid design splits controls across two environments, and keeping policies, logging and configurations aligned is its main security challenge. Losing physical control is wrong because the on-premises servers stay in the company's own facility.

exam_bank.stem: A DevOps team deploys every environment from the same infrastructure as code templates. A template that made a storage bucket publicly readable was copied into all environments before anyone noticed. Which of the following would BEST prevent this in the future?
choices: Apply the templates manually to each environment
Increase the frequency of vulnerability scans in production
Rebuild production servers from golden images every month
Scan templates for misconfigurations before deployment
exam_bank.answer: Scan templates for misconfigurations before deployment
exam_bank.explanation: Because IaC repeats whatever is in the template, checking templates in the pipeline catches a bad setting before it reaches any environment. Scanning production more often only finds the exposure after it is already live.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following BEST describes a serverless architecture?
choices: The provider runs code on demand and manages the servers that execute it
The customer manages virtual machines while the provider manages the hypervisor
Applications are packaged with their dependencies and share the host kernel
A complete application is delivered to users over the internet by a vendor
exam_bank.answer: The provider runs code on demand and manages the servers that execute it
exam_bank.explanation: In serverless computing the customer supplies functions and the provider handles the servers, operating system and scaling. Packaging applications with their dependencies on a shared kernel describes containers, not serverless.

exam_bank.stem: A company split its online store into separate services for catalog, reviews and checkout. When the reviews service crashed during a sale, customers could still browse and pay. Which of the following benefits of a microservices architecture does this show?
choices: Centralized management of a single codebase
exam_bank.explanation: Independently deployed services can fail without taking the rest of the application down. Microservices usually increase the attack surface, because there are more APIs and network connections to secure.

exam_bank.stem: A company keeps its backup management servers on their own switches, and there is no cable or wireless link between those switches and the production network. Which of the following types of network separation is being used?
exam_bank.explanation: Separate hardware with no connection to other networks is physical isolation. Logical segmentation is wrong because it separates traffic on shared hardware using VLANs or rules.

exam_bank.stem: A data center uses software-defined networking, and every switch receives its forwarding rules from one central system. Which of the following components is MOST important to protect, because an attacker who controls it could reconfigure the whole network?
choices: The console port of one router
exam_bank.explanation: The controller is the control plane for every device in an SDN, so compromising it gives control of all forwarding rules. A single edge switch only affects the traffic that passes through that switch.

exam_bank.stem: A network team is choosing between VLANs on shared switches and separate physical networks for a sensitive system. Which of the following is the MAIN security drawback of logical segmentation compared with physical isolation?
choices: A misconfiguration can let traffic cross between segments
It requires separate cabling for every segment
It cannot be combined with firewall rules
It prevents central management of the switches in each segment
exam_bank.answer: A misconfiguration can let traffic cross between segments
exam_bank.explanation: Because logically separated segments share hardware, a configuration mistake or a VLAN hopping attack can allow traffic between them. Separate cabling is a cost of physical isolation, not of logical segmentation.

exam_bank.stem: An attacker with administrator rights on one guest virtual machine exploits a flaw in the hypervisor and gains access to other virtual machines on the same host. Which of the following BEST describes this attack?
exam_bank.explanation: Breaking out of a guest into the hypervisor or other guests is VM escape. Resource reuse is tempting, but it describes leftover data in memory or storage being exposed to a new VM, not an attacker breaking out of a guest.

exam_bank.stem: A development team builds its containers from images pulled from a public registry, and a recent image included a hidden cryptocurrency miner. Which of the following would BEST reduce this risk?
choices: Store the container images on an encrypted volume in the registry
Use only scanned, trusted base images from an approved registry
Increase the memory limits assigned to each container
Run the containers on a type 2 hypervisor
exam_bank.answer: Use only scanned, trusted base images from an approved registry
exam_bank.explanation: The risk comes from untrusted image content, so the fix is to scan images and pull them only from a vetted source. Encrypting the storage protects images from theft but does nothing about malicious code already inside them.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following runs directly on server hardware, with no host operating system underneath it, to host virtual machines?
exam_bank.explanation: A type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor is installed directly on the hardware. A type 2 hypervisor is an application that runs on top of a host operating system.

exam_bank.stem: An electric utility collects readings from substations spread over hundreds of miles and lets operators open and close breakers remotely from a central control room. Which of the following BEST describes this system?
exam_bank.explanation: SCADA is the type of industrial control system that monitors and controls equipment across wide geographic areas from a central site. An RTOS is the operating system inside an individual device, not the supervisory system.

exam_bank.stem: An online retailer's traffic triples during the holiday season. The company wants an architecture that adds capacity automatically during peaks and releases it afterward. Which of the following architecture considerations is the company focused on?
exam_bank.explanation: Scalability is the ability to grow or shrink resources to match demand. Responsiveness is about how quickly the system answers requests, which benefits from scaling but is not the requirement described.

exam_bank.stem: A company is installing battery-powered sensors at remote pipeline sites. The engineers report that the devices cannot run strong encryption or security agents without draining their batteries in days. Which of the following considerations is limiting the security design?
exam_bank.explanation: Small embedded devices have limited power and processing capacity, which restricts which security controls they can run. Ease of deployment is about how simply a system can be rolled out, not whether it can run the controls.

exam_bank.stem: After a breach, an architect wants the company to be able to destroy compromised servers and redeploy clean ones from known-good templates within an hour. Which of the following architecture considerations is the architect prioritizing?
exam_bank.explanation: Ease of recovery is how quickly and reliably a system can be restored after a failure or compromise. Scalability is wrong because the goal is restoring clean systems, not adding capacity.

exam_bank.stem: A company wants an intrusion detection sensor that sees only the attacks that get past its perimeter firewall, without the noise of traffic the firewall already blocks. Where should the sensor be placed?
choices: On the internet-facing link in front of the perimeter firewall
On the internal network directly behind the firewall
exam_bank.answer: On the internal network directly behind the firewall
exam_bank.explanation: A sensor just inside the firewall sees traffic that the firewall allowed, which is where successful attacks show up. A sensor in front of the firewall sees every probe from the internet, including attacks the firewall already stopped.

exam_bank.stem: An audit finds that a VPN concentrator the company stopped using two years ago is still connected to the internet and still has firewall rules allowing traffic to it. Which of the following actions BEST reduces the attack surface?
choices: Move the concentrator to a different public IP address range
Turn on detailed logging on the concentrator
Decommission the concentrator and remove its firewall rules
exam_bank.answer: Decommission the concentrator and remove its firewall rules
exam_bank.explanation: Removing an unused device and its rules eliminates the exposure entirely. Changing the password helps, but the device still offers an internet-facing service that nobody maintains or patches.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following BEST describes a security zone in an enterprise network?
choices: A physical room that requires badge access to enter
A list of applications that are approved to run on a host
A group of systems with similar trust levels that share access rules
A single firewall rule that permits traffic between two specific hosts
exam_bank.answer: A group of systems with similar trust levels that share access rules
exam_bank.explanation: Security zones group systems by trust level, such as internet, screened subnet and internal, with controls enforced between zones. A badge-controlled room is a physical security area, not a network security zone.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the difference between an inline intrusion prevention system and an intrusion detection system connected to a switch's mirror port?
choices: The IDS can block traffic, while the IPS can only alert
The IPS can block traffic, while the IDS can only alert
The IDS adds more latency than the IPS
Only the IPS can use signature-based detection
exam_bank.answer: The IPS can block traffic, while the IDS can only alert
exam_bank.explanation: An inline (active) IPS sits in the traffic path and can drop packets, while a passive IDS receives a copy and can only raise alerts. Both can use signatures, and the passive IDS adds no latency because it is not in the path.

exam_bank.stem: An analyst finds that the switch's mirror port drops packets whenever the network is busy, so the monitoring system misses traffic. Which of the following would BEST capture all traffic reliably without affecting the production link?
exam_bank.explanation: A hardware tap copies every packet passively and is not limited by the switch's mirroring capacity. An inline IPS would see all traffic, but it sits in the path and can affect production if it fails or slows down.

exam_bank.stem: A company wants internet users to reach its internal web servers only through a device that receives their requests, forwards them to the servers and hides the servers' real addresses. Which of the following should be deployed?
exam_bank.explanation: A reverse proxy sits in front of servers and handles inbound requests on their behalf. A forward proxy does the opposite, handling outbound requests from internal clients to the internet.

exam_bank.stem: In an 802.1X deployment, which of the following roles does the network switch perform?
exam_bank.explanation: The switch or access point is the authenticator, passing credentials between the device and the RADIUS server. The supplicant is the client device that requests access.

exam_bank.stem: A company is setting up 802.1X on its wireless network. Only the authentication server will have a certificate, and users will sign in with their username and password inside an encrypted tunnel. Which of the following EAP methods BEST fits?
exam_bank.explanation: PEAP builds a TLS tunnel using only a server certificate and then protects the user's password inside it. EAP-TLS is wrong because it requires a certificate on every client as well.

exam_bank.stem: Visitors keep plugging personal devices into network jacks in a conference room. The company does not have a RADIUS server, and it wants each jack to accept only one known device and shut down if any other device is connected. Which of the following should be configured?
choices: MAC-based port security on the switch
exam_bank.answer: MAC-based port security on the switch
exam_bank.explanation: Switch port security can limit a port to specific MAC addresses and disable it on a violation, with no RADIUS server needed. 802.1X is stronger, but it requires an authentication server, which the company does not have.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following firewall types can identify applications regardless of the port they use, includes intrusion prevention, and can apply rules based on user identity?
exam_bank.explanation: An NGFW adds application awareness, integrated IPS and user-based policy to traditional firewalling. A WAF inspects application traffic too, but only HTTP traffic to web applications, and it does not filter general network traffic.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following is the MAIN limitation of a layer 4 firewall?
choices: It cannot track the state of TCP connections passing through it
It cannot filter traffic by destination port
It cannot be placed inline in the network
It cannot inspect the application content inside allowed ports
exam_bank.answer: It cannot inspect the application content inside allowed ports
exam_bank.explanation: A layer 4 firewall decides based on addresses, ports and protocols, so anything carried over an allowed port passes without content inspection. Stateful layer 4 firewalls do track connection state, so that option is not a limitation.

exam_bank.stem: Remote employees use a VPN that sends only corporate traffic through the tunnel, while their web browsing goes directly to the internet. The security team wants all of their traffic inspected by the corporate web gateway. Which of the following should be configured?
exam_bank.explanation: A full tunnel sends all client traffic through the VPN so it passes the company's security controls. A split tunnel is the current setup, which lets internet traffic bypass the gateway.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following IPSec components encrypts the payload of each packet to provide confidentiality?
exam_bank.explanation: ESP provides encryption, plus integrity and authentication. AH is tempting, but it provides only integrity and authentication, with no encryption.

exam_bank.stem: A manufacturer holds patents on its production process and copyrights on its product design drawings and training videos. Which of the following data types BEST describes these assets?
exam_bank.explanation: Patented and copyrighted creations of the company are intellectual property. Legal information is tempting because patents involve the law, but that type covers records such as contracts and litigation files, not the creations themselves.

exam_bank.stem: A company's legal department stores contracts, records for a pending lawsuit and confidential communications with outside attorneys. Which of the following data types BEST describes these records?
exam_bank.explanation: Contracts, litigation records and attorney communications are legal information. A trade secret is valuable business knowledge kept secret, such as a formula, not records about legal matters.

exam_bank.stem: A finance team handles payroll records, corporate bank account numbers and quarterly earnings figures that have not yet been announced. Which of the following data types BEST describes this data?
exam_bank.explanation: Payroll, banking and earnings data are financial information. Trade secret is the most tempting choice, but earnings figures are protected only until announcement and are not a lasting competitive secret like a formula or process.

exam_bank.stem: A company's policy defines four data labels, from lowest to highest: public, sensitive, confidential and restricted. A plan for an upcoming merger could cause severe damage if leaked, and only board members may see it. Which label should the plan receive?
exam_bank.explanation: The most damaging data, available only to a few named people, belongs at the highest level of the company's scheme, which is restricted. Confidential is close, but the policy reserves a higher level, and this data clearly needs it.

exam_bank.stem: Employee home addresses, salaries and medical leave records should be seen only by the employee and authorized HR staff. Which of the following classifications BEST describes this data?
exam_bank.explanation: Private data relates to individuals and must be protected from disclosure. Proprietary data is information the company owns for its business, such as product plans, rather than personal details about employees.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY reason to classify data before choosing protection controls?
choices: So every data set receives the same level of encryption
So controls can match the value and sensitivity of each data set
So every data set can be deleted after the same retention period
So all backups can be stored in a single location
exam_bank.answer: So controls can match the value and sensitivity of each data set
exam_bank.explanation: Classification tells the organization how much protection each data set needs, so strong controls go where they matter most. Applying the same encryption to everything ignores the differences that classification is meant to identify.

exam_bank.stem: A financial analytics service must keep customer data protected even while it is loaded and decrypted in memory for processing. Which of the following BEST protects the data in this state?
choices: Processing the data inside a secure enclave
Enabling full-disk encryption on the servers
Requiring TLS for all client connections
exam_bank.answer: Processing the data inside a secure enclave
exam_bank.explanation: Data in use sits decrypted in memory, and a secure enclave or trusted execution environment isolates that memory from other processes. Full-disk encryption protects data at rest, not data that is loaded into memory.

exam_bank.stem: A company stores scanned customer contracts in a cloud storage bucket. Auditors want the files protected if the provider's disks were ever stolen or improperly disposed of. Which of the following BEST meets this requirement?
choices: Encrypt the files stored in the bucket
Require TLS for all file uploads
Mask contract numbers in the web interface
Require MFA for all file downloads
exam_bank.answer: Encrypt the files stored in the bucket
exam_bank.explanation: Encrypting stored files protects data at rest on the provider's disks. TLS is tempting, but it protects files only while they travel to the bucket, not once they sit on the disk.

exam_bank.stem: A national privacy law requires that citizens' personal data stay within the country. A company is selecting a SaaS vendor to hold that data. Which of the following should the company verify FIRST?
choices: The vendor's uptime service level agreement
The encryption algorithm the vendor uses for backups
Where the vendor stores and replicates the data
exam_bank.answer: Where the vendor stores and replicates the data
exam_bank.explanation: To meet a data residency requirement, the company must confirm the physical locations of all copies, including replicas and backups. Encryption is important, but it does not change which country's laws apply to where the data is kept.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following BEST describes data sovereignty?
choices: The data owner decides who may access the data
Data must be encrypted whenever it is transferred out of a country
Data must be deleted when its retention period ends
Data is subject to the laws of the country where it is located
exam_bank.answer: Data is subject to the laws of the country where it is located
exam_bank.explanation: Data sovereignty means that data falls under the laws of the nation where it is stored or processed. Deciding who may access data is the data owner's role, which is a different concept.

exam_bank.stem: An employee's account signs in from New York and, 10 minutes later, from Singapore. Which of the following lets the security team flag this activity as suspicious?
choices: Geolocation of the source IP addresses
exam_bank.answer: Geolocation of the source IP addresses
exam_bank.explanation: Mapping each login's IP address to a location shows travel that is physically impossible in that time. Data sovereignty concerns which laws apply to stored data and does not help detect suspicious logins.

exam_bank.stem: A company chooses a cloud backup service that pins all backup copies to one country and never replicates them across borders. Which of the following risks does this choice PRIMARILY address?
choices: The data becoming subject to foreign laws
Ransomware encrypting all of the backup copies
exam_bank.answer: The data becoming subject to foreign laws
exam_bank.explanation: Keeping copies inside one country keeps them under that country's jurisdiction, which is a data sovereignty concern. Ransomware protection depends on immutability or offline copies, not on which country holds the data.

exam_bank.stem: A shared folder that holds payroll spreadsheets turns out to be readable by every employee in the company. Which of the following methods would BEST fix this?
exam_bank.explanation: Limiting the folder's access rights to payroll staff directly removes the unwanted access. Obfuscation only makes data harder to understand, and it would still leave the files available to everyone.

exam_bank.stem: A software company publishes installation files on its website and wants customers to be able to confirm that a downloaded file has not been altered. Which of the following methods should the company use?
exam_bank.explanation: Publishing a hash lets customers compute the hash of their download and compare the two values to confirm integrity. Obfuscation makes code harder to read but gives customers no way to detect changes.

exam_bank.stem: An HR application must store employee identification numbers so that the application can retrieve the original values, but a stolen copy of the database must be unreadable. Which of the following methods BEST meets this requirement?
exam_bank.explanation: Encryption is reversible with the right key, so the application can recover the original values while thieves without the key cannot. Hashing is tempting, but it is one-way, so the original numbers could never be retrieved.

exam_bank.stem: Developers need realistic customer data for testing. The company copies the production database and replaces real names and account numbers with fictitious but consistent values before giving it to them. Which of the following methods is being used?
exam_bank.explanation: Masking replaces sensitive values with realistic substitutes so the data stays usable without exposing real information. Encryption would protect the data, but developers would need the key to use it, which would expose the real values.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following BEST describes an active-passive high availability configuration?
choices: All nodes share the traffic load at the same time
One node handles all traffic while another waits to take over
Traffic is spread across all of the servers by DNS round robin
Backups are copied to a standby server each night
exam_bank.answer: One node handles all traffic while another waits to take over
exam_bank.explanation: In active-passive, the standby node stays idle until the active node fails. Sharing traffic across all nodes at once describes active-active.

exam_bank.stem: Shoppers are being logged out of an online store because the load balancer sends each of their requests to a different web server. Which of the following load balancer settings would BEST fix this?
exam_bank.explanation: Session persistence (affinity) keeps a user's requests on the same server for the length of the session. Round-robin scheduling causes the problem, because it rotates requests across servers.

exam_bank.stem: A company spreads web traffic across six servers, but every request passes through a single load balancer. Which of the following would BEST remove this single point of failure?
choices: Add more web servers behind the existing load balancer
Take nightly snapshots of the load balancer
Add a second load balancer in a redundant pair
Move the load balancer to the screened subnet
exam_bank.answer: Add a second load balancer in a redundant pair
exam_bank.explanation: A redundant load balancer can take over if the first one fails, so the service stays up. Adding web servers improves capacity but leaves the single load balancer as the point of failure.

exam_bank.stem: A small company wants the least expensive recovery site possible. It can tolerate several weeks of downtime and needs only a facility with power, cooling and space for equipment it would buy after a disaster. Which of the following site types BEST fits?
exam_bank.explanation: A cold site provides basic space and utilities with no installed equipment, which makes it the cheapest and slowest option. A warm site already has hardware installed, so it costs more than the company needs to spend.

exam_bank.stem: A payment processor's business impact analysis says its transaction system must resume within minutes of a data center loss. Which of the following recovery site types BEST meets this requirement?
exam_bank.explanation: A hot site runs current systems and data so it can take over almost immediately. A warm site needs time to load recent data, which typically takes hours or days.

exam_bank.stem: A government contractor writes a plan describing how it will keep its essential functions running, including manual workarounds and alternate work locations, during a disruption that could last weeks. Which of the following plans is this?
exam_bank.explanation: A continuity of operations plan focuses on sustaining essential business functions during a prolonged disruption. A disaster recovery plan is tempting, but it focuses on restoring IT systems after a disaster rather than keeping the business running in the meantime.

exam_bank.stem: A company uses one vendor's firewalls at its internet edge and a different vendor's firewalls between its internal zones, so that a single exploit cannot bypass both layers. Which of the following resilience concepts does this BEST describe?
exam_bank.explanation: Using different vendors or technologies means one flaw does not affect every layer. Geographic dispersion is about physical locations, not the variety of products in use.

exam_bank.stem: A company moves from one cloud provider to a multi-cloud design. Which of the following is the MOST likely drawback of this change?
choices: Greater dependence on a single provider
Less resilience to a provider-wide outage
More complexity in managing security across providers
Inability to spread workloads across geographic regions
exam_bank.answer: More complexity in managing security across providers
exam_bank.explanation: Each provider has its own tools, identity systems and settings, which makes consistent security harder to manage. Dependence on one provider is the problem multi-cloud reduces, so it is not a drawback.

exam_bank.stem: A company's VPN software is licensed for 200 concurrent users. When an emergency sent 1,500 employees home, most of them could not connect. Which of the following areas of capacity planning was overlooked?
exam_bank.explanation: The limit was in a software system and its licenses, which falls under technology capacity. Infrastructure is tempting, but in this context it refers to facilities, power and network circuits rather than application licenses.

exam_bank.stem: A company plans to add more server racks to its data center, but an assessment finds the room's cooling and electrical circuits cannot support any additional load. Which of the following areas of capacity planning does this finding affect?
exam_bank.explanation: Power, cooling and facility space are infrastructure capacity. Technology covers the servers and software themselves, which are not what is lacking here.

exam_bank.stem: Only one network engineer knows how to configure the company's core routers, and that engineer is about to go on extended leave. Which of the following is the BEST way to reduce this resilience risk?
choices: Cross-train other staff on the critical tasks
Increase the frequency of configuration backups
exam_bank.answer: Cross-train other staff on the critical tasks
exam_bank.explanation: Cross-training addresses people capacity by making sure more than one person can perform critical work. Backing up the configurations is useful, but no one would know how to apply them if something broke.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following BEST describes capacity planning as part of resilience?
choices: Ensuring enough people, technology and infrastructure to meet demand
Deciding how long backup copies must be retained
Testing failover from the primary data center to the secondary site
Ranking data sets by their sensitivity
exam_bank.answer: Ensuring enough people, technology and infrastructure to meet demand
exam_bank.explanation: Capacity planning makes sure staff, systems and facilities can handle both normal and disrupted demand. Failover testing checks that a design works but does not decide how much capacity is needed.

exam_bank.stem: A security team builds an isolated copy of its network, releases harmless test malware that behaves like ransomware, and has responders carry out their actual containment steps. Which of the following types of exercises is this?
exam_bank.explanation: A simulation recreates a realistic event so participants perform real actions without affecting production. A tabletop exercise is only a discussion of the steps, with no hands-on actions.

exam_bank.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY advantage of a tabletop exercise compared with a full failover test?
choices: It measures the actual recovery time of the systems
It confirms that backup data can be restored
It validates the hardware performance at the recovery site
It tests the plan at low cost with no risk to production
exam_bank.answer: It tests the plan at low cost with no risk to production
exam_bank.explanation: A tabletop exercise is a discussion, so it is cheap and cannot disrupt operations. It does not measure real recovery times, which requires actually failing systems over.

exam_bank.stem: A business impact analysis states that a sales database can lose no more than one hour of data, but the database is backed up only once each night. Which of the following should the company do?
choices: Increase the backup frequency to at least hourly
exam_bank.answer: Increase the backup frequency to at least hourly
exam_bank.explanation: How often backups run determines how much data can be lost, so meeting a one-hour recovery point objective requires at least hourly backups. Moving copies offsite protects them from site disasters but does not reduce the data lost between backups.

exam_bank.stem: A company's backup software reports that every job completes successfully, but no one has ever tried to recover data from them. Which of the following is the BEST way to make sure the backups are usable?
exam_bank.explanation: Only a test restore proves the backup data is complete and recoverable. A longer retention period keeps more copies, but they could all be unusable.

exam_bank.stem: A company stores all of its backup copies on a storage device in the same server room as the systems they protect. Which of the following would BEST protect the company if a fire destroyed that room?
choices: Take snapshots of the production servers more often
Add RAID to the backup storage device
Keep a copy of the backups at an offsite location
exam_bank.answer: Keep a copy of the backups at an offsite location
exam_bank.explanation: An offsite copy survives a disaster that destroys the primary site. RAID protects against a single disk failure, not against the loss of the entire room.

exam_bank.stem: A hospital must keep its systems running through utility power outages that could last several days after a major storm. Which of the following BEST meets this requirement?
choices: A generator with a fuel supply
exam_bank.answer: A generator with a fuel supply
exam_bank.explanation: A generator can supply power for as long as it has fuel, which covers outages lasting days. A UPS is tempting, but its batteries last only minutes to hours and are meant to bridge the gap until a generator starts.

exam_bank.stem: Each server in a rack has two power supplies. Which of the following BEST protects the servers if one electrical circuit in the data center fails?
choices: Connect both power supplies to one larger UPS
Add a surge protector to the existing circuit
Replace both supplies with one higher-wattage supply
Connect each power supply to a separate circuit
exam_bank.answer: Connect each power supply to a separate circuit
exam_bank.explanation: Feeding each power supply from a different circuit means the server keeps running if one circuit goes down. A larger UPS on a single circuit still leaves both supplies depending on the same path.

exam_bank.stem: During an extended power outage, a company's backup generator failed to start, and the servers shut down when the UPS batteries ran out. The generator had never been started since it was installed. Which of the following would BEST prevent this from happening again?
choices: Buy a larger UPS for the data center
Test the generator under load on a regular schedule
Add a second utility power feed
Move the servers to a cloud provider
exam_bank.answer: Test the generator under load on a regular schedule
exam_bank.explanation: Regular load testing finds generator problems before a real outage depends on it. A larger UPS only buys more minutes and still depends on the generator for a long outage.
